216:   async #openGadgetInternal(id: string, shareKey?: string,
217:                             configureObservers?: RpcStub<ObserverConfigCallback>)
218:       : Promise<NativeRpcStub<Overseer>> {
219:     let userId = this.#userId.toString();
220:     let profileId = this.#userId.name!;
221:     let overseerId;
222:     try {
223:       overseerId = this.overseers.idFromString(id);
224:     } catch {
225:       throw createOpenGadgetError(OPEN_GADGET_ERROR_CODES.workspaceNotFound);
226:     }
227:     let overseer = this.overseers.get(overseerId);
228: 
229:     // HACK: Detect loss of the connection to the DO by:
230:     // - Pass a callback to overseer.open() which it should call when the session is disposed.
231:     // - Detect if the callback itself is disposed before being called, suggesting the connection
232:     //   was lost.
233:     // If the connection is lost, we abort this I/O context, which kills the WebSocket from the
234:     // client, forcing it to engage its reconnect logic, which should recover.
235:     // TODO: Implement onRpcBroken() in the built-in RPC system, matching Cap'n Web, and use that
236:     //   instead.
237:     // TODO: Consider how to reconnect to one DO without resetting the whole WebSocket. Probably
238:     //   needs new code on the client side. However, typically a client only ever opens one
239:     //   gadget at a time (since each tab is a separate client), so it's probably fine for now.
240:     let closed = false;
241:     let started = false;
242:     let notifyClosed = () => {
243:       closed = true;
244:     };
245:     (notifyClosed as any)[Symbol.dispose] = () => {
246:       if (started && !closed) {
247:         // this.ctx.abort() would be nicer here, but it is still marked experimental in the
248:         // workers runtime.
249:         this.abortSession(new Error(`lost connection to workspace DO (gadget ${id})`));
250:       }
251:     }
252: 
253:     let result;
254:     try {
255:       result = await overseer.open(userId, profileId, notifyClosed, shareKey, configureObservers);
256:     } catch (err) {
257:       // A denial proves this user's listing for the workspace is stale: revocation tries to drop it
258:       // (refreshAffectedCollaboratorListings), but that push is best-effort. Only catches entries
259:       // they click; others stay frozen at revocation, as a disconnected collaborator gets no pushes.
260:       if (getOpenGadgetErrorCode(err) === OPEN_GADGET_ERROR_CODES.workspaceAccessDenied) {
261:         await this.#user.forgetSharedGadget(id);
262:       }
263:       throw err;
264:     }
265:     started = true;
266:     recordAnalytics(this.ctx, this.env, {
267:       event_name: "gadget_opened",
268:       user_id: userId,
269:       gadget_id: id,
270:       source: shareKey ? "share_key" : "direct",
271:     });
272:     return result;
273:   }

394:   async importBlueprint(archive: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>): Promise<string> {
395:     let { metadata, contentLength, content } = await parseBlueprintArchive(archive);
396:     delete metadata.screenshot;
397:     let blueprintId = randomBlueprintId();
398:     let r2Key = `${blueprintId}/${metadata.version}`;
399: 
400:     try {
401:       let fixedLengthStream = new FixedLengthStream(contentLength);
402: 
403:       await Promise.all([
404:         content.pipeTo(fixedLengthStream.writable),
405:         this.env.BLUEPRINT_CONTENT.put(r2Key, fixedLengthStream.readable),
406:       ]);
407: 
408:       let kvRecord: BlueprintKvRecord = {
409:         metadata,
410:         ownerId: this.#userId.toString(),
411:       };
412: 
413:       await this.env.BLUEPRINTS.put(blueprintId, JSON.stringify(kvRecord));
414: 
415:       await this.#user.importBlueprint(blueprintId, metadata);
416: 
417:       recordAnalytics(this.ctx, this.env, {
418:         event_name: "blueprint_imported",
419:         user_id: this.#userId.toString(),
420:         blueprint_id: blueprintId,
421:       });
422: 
423:       return blueprintId;
424:     } catch (err) {
425:       // Try to delete what we uploaded, but don't wait for results becasue there's nothing we
426:       // can do if they fail, and we already have an error to throw.
427:       this.env.BLUEPRINTS.delete(blueprintId);
428:       this.env.BLUEPRINT_CONTENT.delete(r2Key);
429:       throw err;
430:     }
431:   }

433:   async newGadgetFromBlueprint(
434:     blueprintId: string,
435:     bindings: Record<string, BlueprintBindingAssignment>
436:   ): Promise<RpcStub<Overseer>> {
437:     // 1. Read blueprint from KV.
438:     let kvRecord = await readBlueprintKvRecord(this.env, blueprintId);
439:     if (!kvRecord) throw new Error("Blueprint not found.");
440: 
441:     // 2. Read gzip-compressed Yjs doc from R2 and decompress.
442:     let codeBytes = await readBlueprintContent(this.env, blueprintId, kvRecord.metadata.version);
443:     if (!codeBytes) throw new Error("Blueprint content not found in R2.");
444: 
445:     // 3. Create new Overseer DO (same as newGadget()).
446:     let id = this.overseers.newUniqueId().toString();
447:     await this.#user.newGadget(id, kvRecord.metadata.title);
448:     let overseerResult = await this.#openGadgetInternal(id);
449: 
450:     // 4. Initialize from blueprint code.
451:     let overseerDo = this.overseers.get(this.overseers.idFromString(id));
452:     await overseerDo.initializeFromBlueprint(codeBytes, kvRecord.metadata.title,
453:         deploymentOutputForBlueprint(await readAdminConfig(this.env), blueprintId,
454:             sanitizeBlueprintOutput(kvRecord.metadata.output)));
455: 
456:     // 5. Create gatekeepers from assignments and bind them into the workspace's (only) gadget.
457:     let metadata = await overseerResult.getMetadata();
458:     using gadget = await overseerResult.getGadget(metadata.defaultGadgetId!);
459: 
460:     // Defensively put blueprint bindings into a map (not a raw object) until we've had a chance to
461:     // validate the names.
462:     let blueprintBindings = new Map(Object.entries(kvRecord.metadata.bindings));
463:     let gadgetId = metadata.defaultGadgetId!;
464: 
465:     // Create gatekeepers in two phases: first every non-spawner binding (binding the
466:     // non-spawnerOnly ones into the gadget, and recording each created gatekeeper's id by
467:     // binding name), then the agent spawners, whose configs reference the phase-one results
468:     // symbolically (see SpawnerEnvTarget).
469:     let createdIds = new Map<string, WorkpieceId>();
470:     let gkPromises: Promise<void>[] = [];
471: 
472:     for (let [bindingName, assignment] of Object.entries(bindings)) {
473:       let blueprintBinding = blueprintBindings.get(bindingName);
474:       if (!blueprintBinding) {
475:         throw new Error(`Unknown binding name: ${bindingName}`);
476:       }
477: 
478:       gkPromises.push((async () => {
479:         let gk;
480:         if (assignment.type === "gatekeeper") {
481:           gk = await overseerResult.newGatekeeper(assignment.accountId, assignment.resourceUrl);
482:           if (!gk) {
483:             throw new Error(`Failed to create gatekeeper for binding "${bindingName}".`);
484:           }
485:         } else if (assignment.type === "aiModel") {
486:           gk = await overseerResult.newAiModelGatekeeper(assignment.modelId);
487:         } else {
488:           return;  // agent spawners are created in phase two
489:         }
490:         try {
491:           let id = await gk.getId();
492:           createdIds.set(bindingName, id);
493:           // A spawnerOnly binding exists purely to feed some spawner's env; it is not bound
494:           // into the gadget itself.
495:           if (!blueprintBinding.spawnerOnly) {
496:             await gadget.bind(bindingName, id);
497:           }
498:         } finally {
499:           gk[Symbol.dispose]();
500:         }
501:       })());
502:     }
503: 
504:     await Promise.all(gkPromises);
505: 
506:     // Phase two: agent spawners, with the full AgentSpawnerConfig reconstructed -- displayName
507:     // from the binding's title, modelId from the assignment, and env resolved against the
508:     // phase-one gatekeepers and the new gadget.
509:     for (let [bindingName, assignment] of Object.entries(bindings)) {
510:       if (assignment.type !== "agentSpawner") continue;
511:       let blueprintBinding = blueprintBindings.get(bindingName);
512:       if (blueprintBinding?.type !== "agentSpawner") {
513:         throw new Error(`Binding "${bindingName}" type mismatch.`);
514:       }
515: 
516:       let env: Record<string, WorkpieceId> = {};
517:       for (let [envName, target] of Object.entries(blueprintBinding.env)) {
518:         if (target.type === "gadget") {
519:           env[envName] = gadgetId;
520:         } else {
521:           let id = createdIds.get(target.name);
522:           if (id === undefined) {
523:             throw new Error(`Agent spawner binding "${bindingName}" references binding ` +
524:                 `"${target.name}", which was not assigned.`);
525:           }
526:           env[envName] = id;
527:         }
528:       }
529: 
530:       let config: AgentSpawnerConfig = {
531:         displayName: blueprintBinding.title,
532:         modelId: assignment.modelId,
533:         env,
534:       };
535:       using gk = await overseerResult.newAgentSpawnerGatekeeper(config);
536:       await gadget.bind(bindingName, await gk.getId());
537:     }
538: 
539:     recordAnalytics(this.ctx, this.env, {
540:       event_name: "gadget_created",
541:       user_id: this.#userId.toString(),
542:       gadget_id: id,
543:       blueprint_id: blueprintId,
544:       source: "blueprint",
545:     });
546: 
547:     // @ts-expect-error Cap'n Web RPC stubs and native RPC stubs are compatible but the type
548:     //     system doesn't know this.
549:     return overseerResult;
550:   }

621: // result through a capability (this stub) rather than a guessable id — no login id is ever exposed
622: // to the client. Disposing the stub (e.g. when the pop-up closes or the component unmounts) cancels
623: // the in-flight wait and lets the DO be evicted.

630:   async wait(): Promise<string> {
631:     return await this.pending.awaitResult();

633: }

639:   constructor(private ctx: ExecutionContext, private env: Env,
640:       private abortSession: (reason: Error) => void,
641:       private accessPayload?: JWTPayload) {
642:     super();

652:   async startGatekeeperLogin(vendorId: string): Promise<{ url: string; attempt: RpcStub<LoginAttempt> }> {
653:     if (!getAuthGatekeeperAllowlist(this.env).includes(vendorId)) {
654:       throw new Error(`Sign-in via "${vendorId}" is not enabled on this deployment.`);
655:     }
656:     const vendor = getAuthVendorBinding(this.env, vendorId);
657:     if (!vendor) throw new Error(`No such auth gatekeeper: ${vendorId}`);
658:     const desc = await vendor.describe();
659:     if (!desc.providesAuth) throw new Error(`"${vendorId}" does not provide authentication.`);
660: 
661:     // The PendingLogin DO is the rendezvous between this request and the (separate) OAuth-callback
662:     // invocation. The client never sees its id — we hand back an `attempt` stub instead.
663:     const pendingId = this.ctx.exports.PendingLogin.newUniqueId();
664:     const pending = this.ctx.exports.PendingLogin.get(pendingId);
665:     const callback = this.ctx.exports.LoginConnectCallbackImpl(
666:         { props: { pendingId: pendingId.toString(), vendorId } });
667:     // For most providers, sign-in needs only minimal scopes to verify the user's email (the grant is
668:     // transient); capability scopes are requested later via an explicit connectAccount. Cloudflare is
669:     // the exception: signing in with Cloudflare also links AI Gateway billing, so it requests and
670:     // persists the billing-only scope set up front.
671:     const options = vendorId === CLOUDFLARE_VENDOR_ID
672:       ? { scopes: "full" as const, resourceUrlPatterns: [] }
673:       : { scopes: "auth" as const };
674:     const { url } = await vendor.connectAccount(callback, options);
675:     // @ts-expect-error Cap'n Web RPC stubs and native RPC targets are compatible but the type
676:     //     system doesn't know this.
677:     return { url, attempt: new LoginAttemptImpl(pending) };
678:   }

244: async function checkGatekeeperVendorFilter(
245:     vendor: Service<GatekeeperVendor> | Service<GatekeeperUser>,
246:     vendorId: string,
247:     filter: GatekeeperVendorFilter): Promise<boolean> {
248:   try {
249:     if (filter.resourceUrl) {
250:       let resources = await vendor.getSupportedResources();
251:       let matched = false;
252:       for (let resource of resources) {
253:         if (typeof resource.urlPattern !== "string") {
254:           // Guard against gatekeepers returning a non-string urlPattern for now.
255:           //
256:           // TODO: Consider whether this is the API we want for getSupportedResources(). Is URLPattern
257:           //   even the right thing?
258:           throw new Error("Gatekeeper returned non-string urlPattern from getSupportedResources()");
259:         }
260: 
261:         if (new URLPattern(resource.urlPattern).test(filter.resourceUrl)) {
262:           matched = true;
263:           break;
264:         }
265:       }
266:       if (!matched) return false;
267:     }
268: 
269:     return true;
270:   } catch (err) {
271:     // This function is called when iterating over several gatekeepers to filter them. If one of
272:     // them throws we don't want to block the whole list, so instead log the error and assume this
273:     // gatekeeper should be filtered.
274:     logger.warn("gatekeeper filter check failed", {
275:       event: "gatekeeper.filter.check.failed", vendorId, error: err,
276:     });
277:     return false;
278:   }

562: // =======================================================================================
563: // Agent system prompt and tool descriptions
564: 
565: let SYSTEM_PROMPT = `
566: You are a helpful coding assistant tasked with helping users write small personal applications known as "Gadgets". A Gadget is an application that typically serves a single user, or a small group, rather than being public-facing. They may help a user automate part of their job, or just be gadgets the user makes for fun.
567: 
568: # Workspaces
569: 
570: You are working within a "workspace". A workspace contains any number of Gadgets, plus connections to external resources. Each of these is available to you as a named binding in your \`env\` (used with the \`executeCode\` tool, described later). The workspace's current Gadgets, along with each one's files and bindings, are listed later in this prompt with the \`env\` name each one goes by.
571: 
572: A new workspace contains no Gadgets: use the \`createGadget\` tool to create one before writing any code. Most workspaces contain a single Gadget, but the user may ask you to build several Gadgets that work together.
573: 
574: When the user asks for a new Gadget, ALWAYS consider starting from a blueprint. A blueprint is code for a specific type of Gadget that has already been written. The \`listBlueprints\` tool returns a list of available blueprints. If any of them match the user's request, and the user did not explicitly request otherwise, you should create a new gadget starting from a blueprint.
575: 
576: Note that users rarely ask for "a Gadget" in those words. They ask for a thing: a doc, a deck, a tracker, a tool that does X. Any of those is a request for a new Gadget, and so a request to consider a blueprint — including when the workspace already contains a Gadget, which does not make the request an edit to that one.
577: 
578: Tools refer to Gadgets by their binding name in your env: the file tools (\`readFile\`, \`writeFile\`, \`editFile\`) take a \`gadget\` parameter naming the Gadget that owns the file, and \`setGadgetBinding\` takes a \`gadget\` parameter naming the Gadget whose bindings to modify. Some older workspaces have a "default" Gadget (noted in the gadget list) which the file tools fall back to when \`gadget\` is omitted; even so, prefer passing the name explicitly.
579: 
580: # Writing Gadgets
581: 
582: Gadgets execute on a restricted and heavily-sandboxed variant of Cloudflare Workers.
583: 
584: Each Gadget has two main files: client.js and server.js
585: 
586: server.js defines the Gadget's server-side logic, in the form of a Cloudflare Durable Object class. The class must be exported under the name \`Gadget\`. Unlike with normal Durable Objects on Cloudflare, there is no need to export a separate fetch handler; the Gadgets platform automatically takes care of routing requests to the Gadget. The Gadget has access to private storage via the regular Durable Objects KV and SQLite storage APIs. A simple server.js might look like:
587: 
588: \`\`\`
589: import { DurableObject } from "cloudflare:workers";
590: 
591: export class Gadget extends DurableObject {
592:   greet(name) {
593:     return \`Hello, \${name}!\`;
594:   }
595: }
596: \`\`\`
597: 
598: client.js is JavaScript that runs inside the browser to render a client-side user interface. This script runs inside a sandboxed iframe. It can display UI by manipulating the DOM. The client context is initialized with a special global variable called \`gadget\`, which is an RPC stub pointing at the gadget's Durable Object server. This RPC stub is implemented using Cap'n Web, an RPC system from Cloudflare that works similarly to Cloudflare Workers' built-in RPC system, but is able to be used in a browser. In short, methods invoked on the \`gadget\` stub will invoke the same-named method on the Durable Object class. A simple client.js might look like:
599: 
600: \`\`\`
601: let greeting = await gadget.greet("World");
602: document.body.appendChild(document.createTextNode(greeting));
603: \`\`\`
604: 
605: Note that there is no index.html. Instead, client.js must build the entire UI using JavaScript code.
606: 
607: Make Gadget UIs responsive and usable on both desktop and phones by default.
608: 
609: Both the client and server run inside a strictly isolated sandbox. They cannot make requests to the Internet, e.g. by calling \`fetch()\`. Instead, a Gadget communicates with the outside world strictly through its "bindings", that is, the Cloudflare Workers \`env\` API, which code in the Durable Object class can access as \`this.env\`.
610: 
611: Note that the iframe sandbox on the client side prohibits modal popup boxes like alert() and confirm(), so do not use those.
612: 
613: ## Server -> Client callbacks and subscriptions
614: 
615: Note that Cap'n Web is a bidirectional object capability protocol, meaning, among other things, you can pass a function over RPC, in the params or results of another function. This actually passes the function "by reference": the receiving end actually receives an RPC stub, which can be used to call back over RPC to the original function. This, of course, causes the function to become async, even if the original was synchronous.
616: 
617: Using functions this way is a great way to implement real-time updates. The client can "subscribe" to updates, passing a callback function to the server. The server can then call the function asynchronously whenever the state changes (perhaps due to activity of a different client). This technique should be used when implementing multiplayer collaboration.
618: 
619: When implementing such a subscription, it is important to call \`.dup()\` on the callback stub, in order to obtain a long-lived stub. Otherwise, the stub received as a parameter is implicitly disposed at the end of the function. You should also use \`onRpcBroken\` to monitor for client disconnects, like:
620: 
621: \`\`\`
622: async subscribe(callback) {
623:   let callbackDup = callback.dup();
624:   this.subscribers.add(callbackDup);
625:   callbackDup.onRpcBroken(error => {
626:     this.subscribers.delete(callbackDup);
627:   });
628: }
629: \`\`\`
630: 
631: And on the client:
632: 
633: \`\`\`
634: class Callback extends RpcTarget {
635:   update(state) {
636:     // update the UI
637:   }
638: 
639:   [Symbol.dispose]() {
640:     // Connection lost. Resubscribe using new connection.
641:     gadget.subscribe(this);
642:   }
643: }
644: 
645: gadget.subscribe(new Callback());
646: \`\`\`
647: 
648: The top-level \`gadget\` stub survives backend reconnects, and calls made while its replacement is being acquired will wait. However, other capabilities passed over RPC in either direction are disposed on disconnect, and must be re-acquired.
649: 
650: DO NOT import \`RpcTarget\` in client.js. It is already imported.
651: 
652: If you need \`RpcTarget\` in server.js, you can import it from "cloudflare:workers".
653: 
654: ## Design Tips
655: 
656: * ALWAYS store server state in Durable Object storage, not just in memory. Memory is OK to use for caching but users expect not to have their experience disrupted when the server restarts.
657: * If the user asks for a game or any sort of app where multiple users might collaborate, make sure multiple clients can connect at once and broadcast real-time updates to each other.
658: * Clients may frequently reload, and there is no client-side storage, so there is no way to track long-lived "sessions". So, for example, if the user asks for a multiplayer game, you should design it so that any connected client can choose to be any player. If it's turn-based, you can just let any client make any move. If it's concurrent but with distinct players, let each client choose which player they are controlling, including letting multiple clients choose the same player.
659: * If a Gadget contains a README.md file, use it to describe that Gadget at a high level and document anything that future agents (or humans) may need to know when editing the code. You don't need to document details that are obvious from looking at the code, or which most people and agents would know already.
660: 
661: ## Exporting files from Gadgets
662: 
663: Every Gadget UI can be exported to HTML or PDF using platform-owned controls outside the Gadget. Never add print or export UI to a Gadget and never call \`window.print()\`. Browser-mode PDF exports render using print media; HTML, PNG, and JPEG exports render using screen media. When asked to support or improve PDF export, use standard print CSS such as \`@media print\`, \`@page\`, and CSS fragmentation properties so the output remains readable.
664: 
665: During a browser-mode export, client.js is initialized with another special global variable named \`gadgetExportFormatId\`. This variable is only defined during export; during normal interactive rendering, referencing it directly throws a \`ReferenceError\`. Guard access with \`typeof gadgetExportFormatId !== "undefined"\` or read \`globalThis.gadgetExportFormatId\`. Use \`gadgetExportFormatId\` when the Gadget supports multiple HTML, PDF, PNG, or JPEG export variants. Do not declare or import \`gadgetExportFormatId\` in client.js.
666: 
667: The Workshop waits for client.js, including any top-level \`await\`, to finish before capturing a browser-mode export. Use top-level \`await\` when the initial UI must load data or otherwise complete asynchronous rendering before capture. For example:
668: 
669: \`\`\`
670: let report = await gadget.getReport();
671: let exportFormat = globalThis.gadgetExportFormatId;
672: document.body.className = exportFormat === "compact-pdf" ? "compact" : "interactive";
673: document.body.append(renderReport(report));
674: \`\`\`
675: 
676: To add, replace, or disable export formats, server.js may export a class named \`ExportHandler\`, which must extend \`WorkerEntrypoint\`. Its \`getExportFormats(gadget)\` method returns the complete list of formats, and its \`export(gadget, id)\` method returns a \`ReadableStream<Uint8Array>\` for formats whose mode is \`"server"\`. Read any needed Gadget state before \`export()\` returns; do not capture the borrowed \`gadget\` parameter in the returned stream. If \`getExportFormats(gadget)\` returns only browser-mode formats, do not implement \`export(gadget, id)\`. \`export\` is valid as a JavaScript class method name; write it directly as \`async export(gadget, id)\`, without quoting it or using a computed property. Browser mode supports \`text/html\`, \`application/pdf\`, \`image/png\`, and \`image/jpeg\`; server mode supports any media type. Each format must contain a unique non-empty \`id\`, a \`label\`, a \`mode\`, a \`contentType\`, and a \`fileExtension\` beginning with a dot. Returning an empty list disables export. The Workshop supplies default HTML and PDF formats only when server.js does not export \`ExportHandler\` at all.
677: 
678: For example, this replaces the defaults with one browser-mode PDF variant and one server-generated CSV format:

1: // Sign-in via authentication gatekeepers.
2: //
3: // Unlike the normal connect-account flow (which runs for an already-logged-in user), login happens
4: // before we know who the user is. The PublicApi starts a gatekeeper connect flow (in "auth" scope
5: // mode) with a `LoginConnectCallbackImpl` as the callback and a `PendingLogin` DO to bridge the
6: // result back to the waiting browser:
7: //
8: //   1. PublicApi.startGatekeeperLogin(vendorId) creates a PendingLogin DO (keyed by a random DO id),
9: //      hands the gatekeeper a LoginConnectCallbackImpl, and returns {url, attempt}, where `attempt`
10: //      is an RpcStub wrapping the DO (so the client awaits via a capability, never a guessable id).
11: //   2. The browser opens `url` (the gatekeeper's self-closing OAuth popup) and calls
12: //      `attempt.wait()`, which blocks on the PendingLogin DO.
13: //   3. When the gatekeeper finishes, it calls LoginConnectCallbackImpl.complete(user). We read the
14: //      verified email, resolve/create the email-keyed user DO, mint a session, and deliver the token
15: //      to the PendingLogin DO, which resolves the awaiting RPC.
16: //
17: // Sign-in only requests minimal scopes and the gatekeeper grant is transient (it self-destructs
18: // shortly after we read the email) — so login does NOT create a persistent connected account.
19: // Capability access (repos, docs, billing) is granted later when the user explicitly connects the
20: // gatekeeper, which requests the full scopes and persists the connection.

23: import { GatekeeperConnectCallback, GatekeeperUser } from "@gadgets/workshop-shared/gatekeeper";

25: import { CLOUDFLARE_VENDOR_ID } from "../user.js";

28: const logger = createWorkshopLogger("workshop.auth");

30: type PendingResult = { token: string } | { error: string };
31: 
32: /**
33:  * Bridges a login result from the (separate) OAuth-callback invocation back to the waiting browser.
34:  *
35:  * This DO holds no durable storage: a login normally completes within seconds, and the in-flight
36:  * awaitResult() request keeps the DO alive so the in-memory waiter is reachable when deliver()/fail()
37:  * fire. If the attempt is abandoned, the client disposes the awaiting RPC (the `attempt` stub) and
38:  * the DO is simply evicted — no alarm or cleanup needed.
39:  */
40: export class PendingLogin extends DurableObject<Cloudflare.Env> {
41:   // Awaiters from in-flight awaitResult() calls, resolved/rejected when the result arrives.
42:   #waiters: { resolve: (token: string) => void; reject: (err: Error) => void }[] = [];
43:   // Stash for the rare case deliver()/fail() arrives before awaitResult() registers a waiter.
44:   #result?: PendingResult;
45: 
46:   /** Block until the login completes (or fails). */
47:   async awaitResult(): Promise<string> {
48:     if (this.#result) {
49:       const result = this.#result;
50:       this.#result = undefined;  // one-time use
51:       if ("token" in result) return result.token;
52:       throw new Error(result.error);
53:     }
54:     return await new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {
55:       this.#waiters.push({ resolve, reject });

66:       this.#waiters = [];
67:     } else {
68:       this.#result = { token };

73:     if (this.#waiters.length > 0) {

76:     } else {

71:     super(ctx, env);

78:   /**
79:    * Install the format blueprints bundled with this deployment, if that hasn't already happened
80:    * for this exact manifest. Idempotent and cheap: an up-to-date deployment does one string
81:    * comparison and returns.
82:    *
83:    * Written straight into the featured mirror rather than through setBlueprintFeatured(), whose
84:    * authoritative bit lives in the publishing user's DO -- these have no owning user.
85:    *
86:    * Callers are coalesced onto one run, or two isolates racing on a fresh deployment both promote
87:    * the same blueprints, and a duplicated id makes setFormatOrder() reject every reordering.
88:    */
89:   ensureFormatBlueprintsInstalled(): Promise<boolean> {
90:     return this.#installInFlight ??= this.#installFormatBlueprints()
91:         .finally(() => { this.#installInFlight = undefined; });
92:   }
93: 
94:   #installInFlight?: Promise<boolean>;
95: 
96:   // Resolves true once every bundled blueprint is live. A partial install resolves false rather
97:   // than throwing: the caller has nothing to handle, but it does need to know to ask again.
98:   async #installFormatBlueprints(): Promise<boolean> {
99:     let complete = true;
100:     let manifestVersion = formatBlueprintsManifestVersion();
101:     if (this.storage.installedFormatBlueprints.get() !== manifestVersion) {
102:       let installed = await installFormatBlueprints(this.env);
103: 
104:       if (installed.length > 0) {
105:         for (let publicInfo of installed) {
106:           this.storage.featuredBlueprints.put(publicInfo);
107:         }
108:         await this.#writeFeaturedSnapshot();
109:       }
110: 
111:       // Stamped only once the whole manifest is live, so a crash or a single bad archive retries
112:       // next time. Recording a partial install as complete would strand the entries that failed
113:       // until the manifest happened to change again.
114:       complete = installed.length === FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS.length;
115:       if (complete) {
116:         this.storage.installedFormatBlueprints.put(manifestVersion);
117:       }
118:       logger.info("installed bundled format blueprints", {
119:         event: "formats.install.complete",
120:         size: installed.length,
121:         failureCount: FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS.length - installed.length,
122:       });
123:     }
124: 
125:     // Promotion is checked on every run, not just after an install, so a deployment that installed
126:     // before curation existed still ends up offering its bundled formats.
127:     await this.#promoteBundledFormats();
128:     return complete;
129:   }
130: 
131:   // Offer each bundled blueprint as a standard format, once ever. A separate one-shot decision per
132:   // blueprint: re-deriving the list from the manifest would undo an admin's removal on every
133:   // startup, and reinstalling an updated archive must refresh the blueprint without resetting how
134:   // the deployment has chosen to offer it.
135:   //
136:   // The converse isn't handled: a blueprint dropped from the bundle, or given a new blueprintId,
137:   // leaves its record and its promotion behind for an admin to remove by hand. Withdrawing them
138:   // would mean tracking which promotions this installer made, which is worth doing before the
139:   // bundled set ever changes.
140:   async #promoteBundledFormats(): Promise<void> {
141:     let promoted = new Set(this.storage.promotedFormatBlueprints.get());
142:     let pending = FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS.filter(entry => !promoted.has(entry.blueprintId));
143:     if (pending.length === 0) return;
144: 
145:     let config = this.#config();
146:     let known = new Set(config.formats.map(f => f.blueprintId));
147:     let added = pending
148:         .filter(entry => !known.has(entry.blueprintId))
149:         .map(entry => ({blueprintId: entry.blueprintId, enabled: true}));
150:     // Always write, even when every pending format is already in DO storage. That is the retry
151:     // state after a prior KV mirror failure; stamping promotion without writing would strand the
152:     // hot-path mirror on its old config forever.
153:     await this.updateAdminConfig({formats: [...config.formats, ...added]});
154: 
155:     for (let entry of pending) promoted.add(entry.blueprintId);
156:     this.storage.promotedFormatBlueprints.put([...promoted]);
157:   }

159:   async #writeFeaturedSnapshot(): Promise<void> {
160:     let featured = [...this.storage.featuredBlueprints.list()];
161:     await this.env.BLUEPRINTS.put(FEATURED_BLUEPRINTS_KEY, serializeFeaturedBlueprints(featured));
162:   }

164:   // Reconcile the mirrored featured list to match the authoritative bit stored in the owner
165:   // User DO, while also refreshing stale metadata snapshots for featured entries.
166:   async #syncFeaturedMirror(publicInfo: BlueprintPublicInfo, featured: boolean): Promise<void> {
167:     let existing = this.storage.featuredBlueprints.get(publicInfo.id);
168:     let changed = false;
169: 
170:     if (!featured) {
171:       if (existing) {
172:         this.storage.featuredBlueprints.delete(publicInfo.id);
173:         changed = true;
174:       }
175:     } else if (
176:       !existing ||
177:       existing.metadata.version !== publicInfo.metadata.version ||
178:       existing.metadata.lastUpdated.valueOf() !== publicInfo.metadata.lastUpdated.valueOf()
179:     ) {
180:       this.storage.featuredBlueprints.put(publicInfo);
181:       changed = true;
182:     }
183: 
184:     if (changed) {
185:       await this.#writeFeaturedSnapshot();
186:     }
187:   }

189:   async #getOwnerBlueprint(blueprintId: string): Promise<{
190:     // Absent for a blueprint with no owning user, in which case `featureable` is false.
191:     owner: DurableObjectStub<UserDurableObject> | undefined;
192:     publicInfo: BlueprintPublicInfo;
193:     featureable: boolean;
194:   }> {
195:     if (isReservedBlueprintKey(blueprintId)) {
196:       throw new Error('Blueprint not found.');
197:     }
198: 
199:     let raw = await this.env.BLUEPRINTS.get(blueprintId);
200:     if (!raw) {
201:       throw new Error('Blueprint not found.');
202:     }
203: 
204:     let kvRecord = parseBlueprintKvRecord(raw);
205: 
206:     return {
207:       owner: kvRecord.ownerId
208:           ? this.users.get(this.users.idFromString(kvRecord.ownerId))
209:           : undefined,
210:       publicInfo: {
211:         id: blueprintId,
212:         metadata: kvRecord.metadata,
213:       },
214:       // A deployment-installed blueprint (see format-blueprints.ts) has no owning User DO to hold
215:       // the authoritative featured bit, so the owner-anchored toggle doesn't apply -- the same
216:       // answer as an uploaded blueprint. It reaches users through the deployment's curation.
217:       featureable: !!kvRecord.gadgetId && !!kvRecord.ownerId,
218:     };
219:   }

221:   async isBlueprintFeatured(blueprintId: string): Promise<boolean | null> {
222:     let { owner, publicInfo, featureable } = await this.#getOwnerBlueprint(blueprintId);
223:     if (!featureable || !owner) {
224:       return null;
225:     }
226: 
227:     let featured = await owner.isBlueprintFeatured(blueprintId);
228:     if (featured === null) {
229:       return null;
230:     }
231: 
232:     // Heal partial failures before answering so admin reads never observe disagreement.
233:     await this.#syncFeaturedMirror(publicInfo, featured);
234:     return featured;
235:   }

243:     await owner.setBlueprintFeatured(blueprintId, featured);

273:   async #mutateAdminConfig(mutate: (config: AdminConfig) => AdminConfig): Promise<void> {
274:     let previousMutation = this.adminConfigMutationTail;
275:     let release!: () => void;
276:     this.adminConfigMutationTail = new Promise<void>(resolve => { release = resolve; });
277:     await previousMutation;
278:     try {
279:       let current = this.#config();
280:       let next = mutate(current);
281:       this.storage.adminConfig.put(next);
282:       try {
283:         await this.env.BLUEPRINTS.put(ADMIN_CONFIG_KEY, serializeAdminConfig(next));
284:       } catch (error) {
285:         this.storage.adminConfig.put(current);
286:         throw error;
287:       }
288:     } finally {
289:       release();
290:     }
291:   }

327:   // Admin view of the promoted formats: the deployment's curation joined with each blueprint, so
328:   // the panel can show what is being curated and flag entries whose blueprint has been deleted.
329:   async #listFormatConfig(config: AdminConfig): Promise<AdminFormat[]> {
330:     let bundled = new Set(FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS.map(entry => entry.blueprintId));
331: 
332:     // Every entry, not just the offered ones: the panel exists to show what is disabled and what
333:     // points at a deleted blueprint.
334:     return (await listPromotedFormats(this.env, config.formats)).map(
335:         ({entry, metadata, declared, output}) => ({
336:           blueprintId: entry.blueprintId,
337:           blueprintTitle: metadata?.title ?? "",
338:           blueprintDescription: metadata?.description ?? "",
339:           output,
340:           declared,
341:           overrides: entry.overrides,
342:           enabled: entry.enabled,
343:           agentHint: entry.agentHint ?? "",
344:           missing: !metadata,
345:           bundled: bundled.has(entry.blueprintId),
346:         }));

349:   // Read-modify-write one format entry within the DO, so concurrent admin edits can't clobber each
350:   // other. `mutate` returns the replacement list, or null to leave the config untouched.
351:   async #mutateFormats(mutate: (formats: FormatCuration[]) => FormatCuration[] | null)
352:       : Promise<void> {
353:     await this.#mutateAdminConfig(config => {
354:       let next = mutate(config.formats);
355:       // A no-op may be a retry after the prior KV write failed but DO storage succeeded. Mirror the
356:       // current config again so idempotent retries repair that partial failure.
357:       return next ? {...config, formats: next} : config;
358:     });
359:   }

361:   async promoteFormat(blueprintId: string): Promise<void> {
362:     let record = await readBlueprintKvRecord(this.env, blueprintId);
363:     if (!record) {
364:       throw new Error("Blueprint not found.");
365:     }
366:     await this.#mutateFormats(formats => {
367:       // Idempotent so retrying after a KV mirror failure reaches #mutateFormats()'s repair write.
368:       if (formats.some(f => f.blueprintId === blueprintId)) return null;
369:       // A blueprint that declares no output still needs a stable grouping key before the admin can
370:       // name it. Generate that hidden implementation detail here; the panel only asks the admin for
371:       // the human-facing noun, plural and icon.
372:       let declared = sanitizeBlueprintOutput(record.metadata.output);
373:       return [...formats, {
374:         blueprintId,
375:         enabled: true,
376:         ...(declared ? {} : {overrides: {id: defaultOutputFormatId(blueprintId)}}),
377:       }];
378:     });
379:   }

381:   async removeFormat(blueprintId: string): Promise<void> {
382:     // Enforced here, not just in the panel: this is an RPC an admin session can call directly.
383:     // Withdrawing a bundled entry is `enabled: false`, which keeps its overrides, hint and
384:     // position.
385:     if (FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS.some(entry => entry.blueprintId === blueprintId)) {
386:       throw new Error(
387:           "This format ships with the deployment, so it can't be removed. Turn it off instead.");
388:     }
389:     await this.#mutateFormats(formats => {
390:       let next = formats.filter(f => f.blueprintId !== blueprintId);
391:       return next.length === formats.length ? null : next;
392:     });
393:   }

395:   async updateFormat(blueprintId: string, patch: AdminFormatPatch): Promise<void> {
396:     await this.#mutateFormats(formats => formats.map(entry => {
397:       if (entry.blueprintId !== blueprintId) return entry;
398: 
399:       let next: FormatCuration = {...entry};
400:       if (patch.enabled !== undefined) next.enabled = patch.enabled;
401:       if (patch.agentHint !== undefined) {
402:         // Truncated because every hint is repeated in the system prompt on every turn, so an
403:         // over-long one costs tokens on requests nobody connects back to this panel.
404:         let hint = patch.agentHint.trim().slice(0, MAX_AGENT_HINT);
405:         if (hint) next.agentHint = hint; else delete next.agentHint;
406:       }
407:       if (patch.overrides) {
408:         // null reverts a field to the blueprint's own declaration; absent leaves it alone.
409:         let merged: Record<string, unknown> = {...entry.overrides};
410:         for (let [key, value] of Object.entries(patch.overrides)) {
411:           if (value === null) delete merged[key]; else merged[key] = value;
412:         }
413:         let clean = sanitizeOutputOverrides(merged);
414:         if (clean) next.overrides = clean; else delete next.overrides;
415:       }
416:       return next;
417:     }));
418:   }

467:   /**
468:    * Set a gatekeeper's availability atomically (read-modify-write within the DO). Routes by kind: an
469:    * auto-provisioning ("ambient") gatekeeper stores its three-state mode in ambientGatekeeperModes
470:    * (default stored as absence); an ordinary gatekeeper stores a binary enabled/disabled in
471:    * disabledGatekeepers and rejects the ambient-only 'optional'.
472:    */
473:   async setGatekeeperMode(vendorId: string, mode: AmbientGatekeeperMode): Promise<void> {
474:     vendorId = vendorId.toLowerCase();
475:     let vendor = this.vendors.get(vendorId);
476:     let autoProvisions = !!vendor && (await vendor.describe()).autoProvisionsAccount === true;
477:     if (autoProvisions) {
478:       await this.#mutateAdminConfig(config => {
479:         let modes = { ...config.ambientGatekeeperModes };
480:         if (mode === DEFAULT_AMBIENT_GATEKEEPER_MODE) delete modes[vendorId]; else modes[vendorId] = mode;
481:         return { ...config, ambientGatekeeperModes: modes };
482:       });
483:     } else {
484:       if (mode === "optional") {
485:         throw new Error(`"${vendorId}" is not an auto-provisioning gatekeeper; use 'enabled' or 'disabled'.`);
486:       }
487:       await this.#mutateAdminConfig(config => {
488:         let disabled = new Set(config.disabledGatekeepers);
489:         if (mode === "enabled") disabled.delete(vendorId); else disabled.add(vendorId);
490:         return { ...config, disabledGatekeepers: [...disabled] };
491:       });
492:     }
493:   }

495:   // Admin view of every bound gatekeeper's resource types, annotated with their enabled state.
496:   // Unlike the user-facing listGatekeeperVendors, this does NOT hide disabled resources (so admins
497:   // can re-enable them). `adminUserId` is forwarded to getSupportedResources() so RBAC-gated
498:   // gatekeepers still surface for an admin who has access to them.
499:   async #listResourceConfig(config: AdminConfig, adminUserId: string): Promise<AdminResourceVendor[]> {
500:     let disabledGatekeeperSet = new Set(config.disabledGatekeepers);
501: 
502:     let promises: Promise<AdminResourceVendor | null>[] = [];
503:     for (let [id, vendor] of this.vendors) {
504:       promises.push((async () => {
505:         try {
506:           let [description, supportedResources] = await Promise.all([
507:             vendor.describe(),
508:             vendor.getSupportedResources({ userId: adminUserId }),
509:           ]);
510:           if (description.autoProvisionsAccount) {
511:             // Auto-provisioning ("ambient") gatekeeper: a three-state mode, no resources to toggle.
512:             let mode = ambientGatekeeperMode(config, id);
513:             return {
514:               vendorId: id,
515:               displayName: description.displayName,
516:               logo: description.logo,
517:               autoProvisions: true,
518:               ambientMode: mode,
519:             };
520:           }
521:           if (supportedResources.length === 0) {
522:             // Nothing to toggle for this gatekeeper.
523:             return null;
524:           }
525:           let disabled = new Set(config.disabledResources[id] ?? []);
526:           return {
527:             vendorId: id,
528:             displayName: description.displayName,
529:             logo: description.logo,
530:             autoProvisions: false,
531:             enabled: !disabledGatekeeperSet.has(id),
532:             resources: supportedResources.map(r => ({
533:               urlPattern: r.urlPattern,
534:               title: r.title,
535:               description: r.description,
536:               icon: r.icon,
537:               enabled: !disabled.has(r.urlPattern),
538:             })),
539:           };
540:         } catch (err) {
541:           logger.warn("failed to read resource config for gatekeeper", {
542:             event: "gatekeeper.resource.config.read.failed", gatekeeperId: id, error: err,
543:           });
544:           return null;
545:         }
546:       })());
547:     }
548: 
549:     let vendors = (await Promise.all(promises)).filter((v): v is AdminResourceVendor => v !== null);
550:     // Show auto-provisioned ("ambient") gatekeepers first; preserve the existing order otherwise.
551:     vendors.sort((a, b) => Number(b.autoProvisions) - Number(a.autoProvisions));
552:     return vendors;
553:   }
554: }

1: // Installing the deployment's bundled output-format blueprints.
2: //
3: // The archives and their presentation come from a directory chosen at build time (see
4: // scripts/build-format-blueprints.mjs), so a deployment ships its own formats by pointing
5: // FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS_DIR at its own tree rather than by editing this repo.
6: //
7: // Installation writes an ordinary blueprint -- metadata into BLUEPRINTS, the code snapshot into
8: // BLUEPRINT_CONTENT -- exactly as publishing does. Nothing downstream knows these are special:
9: // no reserved id prefix, no fallback branch in the read path. Failure is tolerable: a deployment
10: // with none installed simply has no standard formats.
11: 
12: import { BlueprintMetadata, BlueprintPublicInfo } from "@gadgets/workshop-shared/api";
13: import { BlueprintKvRecord, parseBlueprintArchive } from "./blueprint-archive.js";
14: import { BundledFormatBlueprint, FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS } from "./generated/format-blueprints.js";
15: import { fingerprint } from "./admin-config.js";
16: import { createWorkshopLogger } from "./observability";
17: 
18: const logger = createWorkshopLogger("workshop.formats");
19: 
20: type InstallEnv = Pick<Cloudflare.Env, "BLUEPRINTS" | "BLUEPRINT_CONTENT">;
21: 
22: /**
23:  * Identifies the exact set of bundled blueprints a deployment has installed, and how. Compared
24:  * with what was installed last time, so any change here triggers reinstallation.
25:  *
26:  * Everything that ends up in the installed metadata contributes, not just `revision`: editing a
27:  * description would otherwise build, deploy, and change nothing on a deployment that had already
28:  * installed. `revision` covers the one input this can't see, the archive bytes.
29:  */
30: export function formatBlueprintsManifestVersion(): string {
31:   return FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS
32:       .map(e => `${e.blueprintId}@${e.revision}+` +
33:           fingerprint(JSON.stringify([e.title, e.description, e.author, e.output])))
34:       .toSorted()
35:       .join(",");
36: }
37: 
38: // Install one bundled blueprint, returning its public info for the featured mirror.
39: async function installOne(env: InstallEnv, entry: BundledFormatBlueprint)
40:     : Promise<BlueprintPublicInfo> {
41:   // Parse through the ordinary archive reader so a corrupt bundled file fails the same way an
42:   // uploaded one would, rather than producing a half-installed blueprint.
43:   let {metadata, contentLength, content} = await parseBlueprintArchive(
44:       new Response(Uint8Array.fromBase64(entry.archive) as BufferSource).body!);
45: 
46:   // R2 needs a known length, and the archive is already fully in memory (it came out of the
47:   // Worker bundle), so buffer rather than plumbing a FixedLengthStream through as the upload path
48:   // does for genuinely streamed uploads.
49:   let contentBytes = new Uint8Array(await new Response(content).arrayBuffer());
50:   if (contentBytes.byteLength !== contentLength) {
51:     throw new Error(`Archive declares ${contentLength} content bytes but holds ` +
52:         `${contentBytes.byteLength}.`);
53:   }
54: 
55:   // The archive supplies what the blueprint does -- code, bindings, and the dates from the
56:   // workspace it was exported from. How it is presented comes from its sidecar, overwriting
57:   // whatever the archive carries.
58:   let installed: BlueprintMetadata = {
59:     ...metadata,
60:     title: entry.title,
61:     description: entry.description,
62:     author: entry.author,
63:     output: entry.output,
64:   };
65: 
66:   // Content first: a blueprint whose metadata exists but whose R2 object doesn't is broken, while
67:   // the reverse is merely an orphaned object that the next install overwrites. The archive's
68:   // content section is already gzip-compressed, which is exactly what R2 holds.
69:   await env.BLUEPRINT_CONTENT.put(`${entry.blueprintId}/${installed.version}`, contentBytes);
70: 
71:   let kvRecord: BlueprintKvRecord = {metadata: installed};
72:   await env.BLUEPRINTS.put(entry.blueprintId, JSON.stringify(kvRecord));
73: 
74:   return {id: entry.blueprintId, metadata: installed};
75: }
76: 
77: /**
78:  * Install every bundled blueprint, skipping (and logging) any that fail. Returns the public info
79:  * of those that installed, so the caller can offer them to users.
80:  */
81: export async function installFormatBlueprints(env: InstallEnv): Promise<BlueprintPublicInfo[]> {
82:   let installed: BlueprintPublicInfo[] = [];
83:   for (let entry of FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS) {
84:     try {
85:       installed.push(await installOne(env, entry));
86:       logger.info("installed format blueprint", {
87:         event: "formats.install.ok", blueprintId: entry.blueprintId,
88:       });
89:     } catch (err) {
90:       // One bad archive must not deny the deployment the others.
91:       logger.error("failed to install format blueprint", {
92:         event: "formats.install.failed", blueprintId: entry.blueprintId, error: err,
93:       });
94:     }
95:   }
96:   return installed;
97: }

124:     if (error instanceof Error &&
125:         (error.message === `Worker has no such entrypoint: ${GADGET_EXPORT_ENTRYPOINT}` ||
126:           error.message.startsWith("internal error"))) {
127:       return null;
128:     }
129:     throw error;
130:   } finally {
131:     deadline.clear();
132:   }

136: export async function exportServerFormat(
137:   createStream: () => Promise<ReadableStream<Uint8Array>>,
138: ): Promise<ReadableStream<Uint8Array>> {
139:   const deadline = createExportDeadline("Gadget export timed out.");

143:     return limitExportStream(source, deadline);
144:   } catch (error) {
145:     deadline.clear();
146:     void streamPromise.then(stream => stream.cancel(error), () => {}).catch(() => {});

1: // The workspace git object store.
2: //
3: // Each workspace's Overseer DO holds a real git object database -- SHA-1, zlib-deflated loose
4: // objects, byte-identical to what `git` itself would write -- stored in the `gitObjects`
5: // typed-storage collection. Mainline gadget code is (will be, once the commit-backed code flow
6: // lands) represented as commits in this store, with each GadgetRecord pointing at its head
7: // commit.
8: //
9: // There is deliberately no ref layer: no branches, tags, or HEAD. Our "refs" are the gadget
10: // records, blueprint records, and chats' pinned commits, all managed by the Overseer's own
11: // workflow. Because the store is content-addressed and refless, unrelated histories coexist
12: // freely in the same collection, and related histories (gadgets forked from each other or
13: // instantiated from the same blueprint) deduplicate at the blob/tree level.
14: //
15: // We use real git formats (rather than a git-shaped custom encoding) so that gadget code can
16: // later be exported to and imported from real git repositories, and so agents can eventually
17: // "mount" arbitrary repos through gatekeeper-gated push/pull. isomorphic-git provides the object
18: // codec; we use only its plumbing (writeBlob/writeTree/writeCommit/read*/log), which operates
19: // against a gitdir containing nothing but `objects/**`. The porcelain is off-limits:
20: // `git.commit` requires HEAD/index/config, and `git.merge` cannot represent the merge behavior
21: // we want (see `threeWayMerge`).
22: //
23: // Storage notes:
24: // - Loose objects only, one collection record per object, keyed by oid. isomorphic-git never
25: //   writes deltified data (it only reads deltas in packfiles fetched from remotes), so each
26: //   record is a zlib'd whole object. Dedup comes from content addressing, not deltas.
27: // - No object exceeds ~2MB today (records hold single source files, small trees, and commit
28: //   headers). If large blobs ever appear, chunking records or spilling to R2 is a change local
29: //   to the fs shim below.
30: // - No GC. Dangling objects are only created by accepted merges, imports, and migration -- never
31: //   by in-flight chats -- and are cheap. If GC is ever needed, the roots are enumerable: gadget
32: //   records, blueprint gadget records, live chats' pinned commits, the pin declarations in chat
33: //   logs and compaction checkpoints (closed epochs are reconstructed from them), and the
34: //   `observedCommit` stamps on chats' readFile tool calls (which nothing else roots -- a future
35: //   GC must either root them or the agent's elision path must tolerate a missing commit by
36: //   eliding unconditionally).
37: 
38: import {
39:   readBlob,
40:   readCommit,
41:   readTree,
42:   writeBlob,
43:   writeCommit,
44:   writeTree,
45:   log,
46:   type PromiseFsClient,
47:   type TreeEntry,
48: } from "isomorphic-git";
49: import diff3Merge from "diff3";
50: import { collection, type Collection } from "@gadgets/typed-storage";
51: import type { AiChatAuthorInfo, CommitIdentity, CommitInfo } from "@gadgets/workshop-shared/api";
52: 
53: // =======================================================================================
54: // Storage schema
55: 
56: /**
57:  * One git loose object: `data` is the zlib-deflated object exactly as git would store it under
58:  * `.git/objects/xx/yyyy...`, and `oid` is its 40-hex SHA-1 name. Content-addressed, hence
59:  * immutable and idempotent to rewrite.
60:  */
61: export interface GitObjectRecord {
62:   oid: string;
63:   data: Uint8Array;
64: }
65: 
66: /**
67:  * Typed-storage schema for a git object store collection. Shared between `makeOverseerStorage()`
68:  * and tests so both bind the identical schema.
69:  */
70: export function gitObjectsCollection() {
71:   return collection<GitObjectRecord>()({
72:     primaryKey: "oid",
73:   });
74: }
75: 
76: // =======================================================================================
77: // fs shim
78: //
79: // isomorphic-git's only storage interface is a filesystem. We give it a virtual one that maps
80: // loose-object paths onto the `gitObjects` collection and rejects everything else, so we never
81: // silently accept writes we didn't intend to store. If we ever need non-object paths (e.g. for
82: // git protocol support), that's a schema extension we design then.
83: 
84: /** The virtual gitdir path the fs shim serves. Only meaningful within this module and tests. */
85: export const GITDIR = "/git";
86: 
87: const LOOSE_OBJECT_PATH = new RegExp(`^${GITDIR}/objects/([0-9a-f]{2})/([0-9a-f]{38})$`);
88: 
89: /** Parses a loose-object path within the virtual gitdir into its 40-hex oid. */
90: function oidFromLoosePath(path: unknown): string | undefined {
91:   if (typeof path !== "string") return undefined;
92:   let match = LOOSE_OBJECT_PATH.exec(path);
93:   if (!match) return undefined;
94:   return match[1] + match[2];
95: }

97: /** Makes an Error carrying the `code` property Node-style fs consumers dispatch on. */
98: function fsError(code: string, message: string): Error {
99:   return Object.assign(new Error(`${code}: ${message}`), { code });

102: /**
103:  * A `PromiseFsClient` backed by a `gitObjects` collection. Exposed for tests; production code
104:  * should use `GitStore`.
105:  *
106:  * Contract subtleties, verified against isomorphic-git 1.40:
107:  * - All ten methods must exist even though only `readFile`/`writeFile`/`stat`/`mkdir`/`readdir`
108:  *   are ever exercised for object-database work: `bindFs` binds every one unconditionally.
109:  * - The promise-style detection probe calls `readFile()` with no arguments and requires a
110:  *   promise back; `async` methods satisfy this by returning a rejected promise rather than
111:  *   throwing synchronously.
112:  * - Missing files must reject with `code: "ENOENT"`: `FileSystem.exists()` rethrows anything
113:  *   else, and `discoverGitdir` / `FileSystem.read` / `FileSystem.readdir` tolerate rejections
114:  *   (the gitdir itself, `shallow`, and `objects/pack` reads all take those paths).
115:  */
116: export function makeGitObjectsFs(objects: Collection<GitObjectRecord, string>): PromiseFsClient {
117:   return { promises: {
118:     async readFile(path: unknown): Promise<Uint8Array> {
119:       let oid = oidFromLoosePath(path);
120:       if (oid === undefined) throw fsError("ENOENT", `unsupported read: ${String(path)}`);
121:       let record = objects.get(oid);
122:       if (record === undefined) throw fsError("ENOENT", `no such object: ${oid}`);
123:       return record.data;
124:     },
125: 
126:     async writeFile(path: unknown, data: unknown): Promise<void> {
127:       let oid = oidFromLoosePath(path);
128:       if (oid === undefined) throw fsError("EPERM", `unsupported write: ${String(path)}`);
129:       if (!(data instanceof Uint8Array)) throw fsError("EINVAL", "expected binary object data");
130:       // Copy: the input is typically a Buffer view over a shared pool, and the record outlives
131:       // the call.
132:       objects.put({ oid, data: new Uint8Array(data) });
133:     },
134: 
135:     async stat(path: unknown): Promise<{
136:       isFile(): boolean;
137:       isDirectory(): boolean;
138:       isSymbolicLink(): boolean;
139:       size: number;
140:     }> {
141:       // Only existing loose objects stat successfully. The gitdir itself rejecting is fine:
142:       // discoverGitdir treats a failed stat as "neither file nor directory" and uses the path
143:       // as-is.
144:       let oid = oidFromLoosePath(path);
145:       let record = oid === undefined ? undefined : objects.get(oid);
146:       if (record === undefined) throw fsError("ENOENT", `no such file: ${String(path)}`);
147:       let size = record.data.byteLength;
148:       return {
149:         isFile: () => true,
150:         isDirectory: () => false,
151:         isSymbolicLink: () => false,
152:         size,

154:     },
155: 
156:     async mkdir(_path: unknown): Promise<void> {
157:       // Directories don't exist in this store; object writes succeed without them. Accept and
158:       // ignore so `FileSystem.write`'s mkdirp fallback can't fail.
159:     },
160:

162:       // The packed-object probe lists `objects/pack`; we store no packfiles, so it's empty.
163:       if (path === `${GITDIR}/objects/pack`) return [];
164:       throw fsError("ENOENT", `unsupported readdir: ${String(path)}`);
165:     },
166: 
167:     // Never used for object-database work, but bindFs requires them to exist.
168:     async lstat(path: unknown): Promise<never> {
169:       throw fsError("ENOSYS", `lstat unsupported by git-store: ${String(path)}`);
170:     },
171:     async unlink(path: unknown): Promise<never> {
172:       throw fsError("ENOSYS", `unlink unsupported by git-store: ${String(path)}`);
173:     },
174:     async rmdir(path: unknown): Promise<never> {
175:       throw fsError("ENOSYS", `rmdir unsupported by git-store: ${String(path)}`);
176:     },
177:     async readlink(path: unknown): Promise<never> {
178:       throw fsError("ENOSYS", `readlink unsupported by git-store: ${String(path)}`);
179:     },
180:     async symlink(path: unknown): Promise<never> {
181:       throw fsError("ENOSYS", `symlink unsupported by git-store: ${String(path)}`);
182:     },
183:   } };
184: }

186: // =======================================================================================
187: // GitStore
188: 
189: /** Options for `GitStore.writeFilesAsCommit()`. */
190: export interface WriteCommitOptions {
191:   /** Parent commit oids; empty for a root commit. */
192:   parents: string[];
193: 
194:   /** Commit author. Also used as the committer unless `committer` is given. */
195:   author: CommitIdentity;
196: 
197:   /** Committer, when distinct from the author. */
198:   committer?: CommitIdentity;
199: 
200:   /** Commit message. Normalized git-style to end with exactly one newline. */
201:   message: string;
202: 
203:   /** Author and committer timestamp. Recorded in UTC (timezone offset 0). */
204:   timestamp: Date;
205: }
206: 
207: // A parsed-but-unwritten tree: file contents at the leaves, subtrees within.
208: type TreeNode = Map<string, TreeNode | string>;
209: 
210: /**
211:  * A git object database over a `gitObjects` collection.
212:  *
213:  * This is plumbing only: it reads and writes blobs/trees/commits by oid and knows nothing about
214:  * refs -- callers (gadget records, blueprint records, chat pins) track which commits matter.
215:  * Files are presented as flat `path -> text` maps; paths may contain `/`, which maps to nested
216:  * trees so stored history stays interoperable with real git tooling.
217:  *
218:  * Construct one per Overseer instance and reuse it: it carries isomorphic-git's parse cache.
219:  */
220: export class GitStore {
221:   #fs: PromiseFsClient;
222:   #cache: object = {};
223: 
224:   constructor(objects: Collection<GitObjectRecord, string>) {
225:     this.#fs = makeGitObjectsFs(objects);
226:   }
227: 
228:   /**
229:    * Writes `files` (a `path -> text` map) as a commit, returning the commit oid. All objects are
230:    * content-addressed, so rewriting identical content is a cheap no-op that produces the same
231:    * oids.
232:    */
233:   async writeFilesAsCommit(
234:       files: ReadonlyMap<string, string>, options: WriteCommitOptions): Promise<string> {
235:     let tree = await this.#writeTreeNode(buildTreeNode(files));
236:     let when = { timestamp: Math.floor(options.timestamp.getTime() / 1000), timezoneOffset: 0 };
237:     return await writeCommit({
238:       fs: this.#fs,
239:       gitdir: GITDIR,
240:       commit: {
241:         message: options.message,
242:         tree,
243:         parent: [...options.parents],
244:         author: { ...options.author, ...when },
245:         committer: { ...(options.committer ?? options.author), ...when },
246:       },
247:     });
248:   }
249: 
250:   /**
251:    * Reads back the full file map of a commit: the inverse of `writeFilesAsCommit()`, with nested
252:    * trees flattened to `/`-joined paths.
253:    *
254:    * Only regular-file blobs (modes 100644/100755) are supported; symlinks and submodules --
255:    * which we never write, but an imported history could contain -- are rejected rather than
256:    * misread.
257:    */
258:   async readCommitFiles(oid: string): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
259:     let { commit } = await readCommit({ fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, oid, cache: this.#cache });
260:     let files = new Map<string, string>();
261:     await this.#collectTreeFiles(commit.tree, "", files);
262:     return files;
263:   }
264: 
265:   /**
266:    * Reads a commit's tree as a `path -> blob oid` map (flattened like `readCommitFiles`, but
267:    * without touching blob content). Content addressing makes this the cheap way to ask which
268:    * files differ between two commits -- see `changedPaths`.
269:    */
270:   async commitFileOids(oid: string): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
271:     let { commit } = await readCommit({ fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, oid, cache: this.#cache });
272:     let out = new Map<string, string>();
273:     await this.#collectTreeOids(commit.tree, "", out);
274:     return out;
275:   }
276: 
277:   /**
278:    * The set of file paths whose content differs between two commits' trees (added, removed, or
279:    * changed), compared by oid -- equal subtrees short-circuit without descending, and no blob
280:    * content is ever read. `undefined` on either side means an empty tree, so a one-sided call
281:    * lists a commit's whole tree.
282:    */
283:   async changedPaths(a: string | undefined, b: string | undefined): Promise<Set<string>> {
284:     let changed = new Set<string>();
285:     if (a === b) return changed;
286:     let treeOf = async (oid: string | undefined) => oid === undefined ? undefined
287:         : (await readCommit({ fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, oid, cache: this.#cache }))
288:             .commit.tree;
289:     await this.#diffTrees(await treeOf(a), await treeOf(b), "", changed);
290:     return changed;
291:   }
292: 
293:   // Accumulates the paths that differ between two trees (either may be absent = empty) into
294:   // `out`. Entries are matched by name; a name that is a blob on one side and a tree on the
295:   // other contributes every path under both sides.
296:   async #diffTrees(aOid: string | undefined, bOid: string | undefined, prefix: string,
297:                    out: Set<string>): Promise<void> {
298:     if (aOid === bOid) return;
299:     let entriesOf = async (oid: string | undefined) => {
300:       if (oid === undefined) return new Map<string, TreeEntry>();
301:       let { tree } = await readTree({ fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, oid, cache: this.#cache });
302:       return new Map(tree.map(entry => [entry.path, entry]));
303:     };
304:     let aEntries = await entriesOf(aOid);
305:     let bEntries = await entriesOf(bOid);
306:     for (let name of new Set([...aEntries.keys(), ...bEntries.keys()])) {
307:       let a = aEntries.get(name);
308:       let b = bEntries.get(name);
309:       if (a?.oid === b?.oid && a?.type === b?.type) continue;
310:       let path = prefix + name;
311:       if (a?.type === "tree" || b?.type === "tree") {
312:         // Descend the tree side(s); a blob opposite a tree is one more difference at `path`.
313:         await this.#diffTrees(a?.type === "tree" ? a.oid : undefined,
314:                               b?.type === "tree" ? b.oid : undefined, `${path}/`, out);
315:         if (a?.type === "blob" || b?.type === "blob") out.add(path);
316:       } else {
317:         out.add(path);
318:       }
319:     }
320:   }
321: 
322:   /**
323:    * Walks the commit graph from `oid` (the commit itself first, then its ancestry), returning up
324:    * to `depth` commits' metadata. Traversal order for merge commits follows git log's default
325:    * (reverse chronological).
326:    */
327:   async readCommitLog(oid: string, options: { depth?: number } = {}): Promise<CommitInfo[]> {
328:     let entries = await log({
329:       fs: this.#fs,
330:       gitdir: GITDIR,
331:       ref: oid,
332:       depth: options.depth,
333:       cache: this.#cache,
334:     });
335:     return entries.map(entry => ({
336:       oid: entry.oid,
337:       parents: entry.commit.parent,
338:       message: entry.commit.message,
339:       author: { name: entry.commit.author.name, email: entry.commit.author.email },
340:       timestamp: new Date(entry.commit.author.timestamp * 1000),
341:     }));
342:   }
343: 
344:   async #writeTreeNode(node: TreeNode): Promise<string> {
345:     let entries: TreeEntry[] = [];
346:     for (let [name, child] of node) {
347:       if (typeof child === "string") {
348:         let oid = await writeBlob({
349:           fs: this.#fs,
350:           gitdir: GITDIR,
351:           blob: new TextEncoder().encode(child),
352:         });
353:         entries.push({ mode: "100644", path: name, oid, type: "blob" });
354:       } else {
355:         let oid = await this.#writeTreeNode(child);
356:         entries.push({ mode: "040000", path: name, oid, type: "tree" });
357:       }
358:     }
359:     // isomorphic-git sorts entries into git's canonical tree order itself.
360:     return await writeTree({ fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, tree: entries });
361:   }
362: 
363:   // The oid-level analog of #collectTreeFiles: flattens a tree to `path -> blob oid` without
364:   // reading any blob. Applies the same mode restriction, so the two views can never disagree
365:   // about which paths exist.
366:   async #collectTreeOids(
367:       treeOid: string, prefix: string, out: Map<string, string>): Promise<void> {
368:     let { tree } = await readTree(
369:         { fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, oid: treeOid, cache: this.#cache });
370:     for (let entry of tree) {
371:       let path = prefix + entry.path;
372:       if (entry.type === "tree") {
373:         await this.#collectTreeOids(entry.oid, `${path}/`, out);
374:       } else if (entry.type === "blob" && (entry.mode === "100644" || entry.mode === "100755")) {
375:         out.set(path, entry.oid);
376:       } else {
377:         throw new Error(`unsupported tree entry at ${path}: mode ${entry.mode}`);
378:       }
379:     }
380:   }
381: 
382:   async #collectTreeFiles(
383:       treeOid: string, prefix: string, out: Map<string, string>): Promise<void> {
384:     let { tree } = await readTree(
385:         { fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, oid: treeOid, cache: this.#cache });
386:     for (let entry of tree) {
387:       let path = prefix + entry.path;
388:       if (entry.type === "tree") {
389:         await this.#collectTreeFiles(entry.oid, `${path}/`, out);
390:       } else if (entry.type === "blob" && (entry.mode === "100644" || entry.mode === "100755")) {
391:         let { blob } = await readBlob(

396:       }

401: // Converts a flat `path -> text` map into nested tree nodes, validating path shape as we go:
402: // git can't represent empty segments or "."/"..", and a path can't be both a file and a
403: // directory.
404: function buildTreeNode(files: ReadonlyMap<string, string>): TreeNode {
405:   let root: TreeNode = new Map();
406:   for (let [path, content] of files) {

3: // This module owns all manipulation of the `collaborators` and `shareKeys` storage collections
4: // and the permission graph that links them. It deliberately performs no RPC: anything that
5: // requires talking to a User DO (resolving a profile from a username, fetching the owner's
6: // profile, notifying a user that a gadget was opened, etc.) stays in the Overseer, which passes
7: // resolved values (or, where laziness matters, a callback) into this module.
8: //
9: // LAZY REVOCATION MODEL: Access is determined by reachability from the owner in the permission
10: // graph, recomputed live at every open() (see `getEffectiveRole`). Revocation is therefore lazy:
11: // removing a collaborator only severs the edges granting *them* access, and revoking a share link
12: // only flags the link revoked. Nothing cascades, no records are deleted, and downstream edges are
13: // never touched -- users who lose their only path to the owner simply become unreachable and are
14: // denied at open() time. Because the graph is never destructively pruned, revocation is reversible:
15: // re-adding a removed collaborator restores them and, transitively, everyone they had shared with.
