106: /**
107:  * Another key for an existing link, minted when the user copies it. Carries no metadata of its
108:  * own: redeeming it resolves to the link record, so all of a link's keys behave identically.
109:  */
110: export type ShareKeyAliasRecord = {
111:   id: string;        // HMAC-SHA-256 hex of the raw key
112:   alias: string;     // id of the link this key is a copy of
113: };
114: 
115: /**
116:  * A row of the share keys table: either a link or a copy of one. Because a link is itself a key
117:  * record, keys written before copies existed are already valid links -- no migration needed.
118:  */
119: export type ShareKeyRecord = ShareLinkRecord | ShareKeyAliasRecord;
120: 
121: /**
122:  * The slice of Overseer storage this module operates on. Satisfied by the real OverseerStorage
123:  * and easily constructed over a Map-backed mock DurableObjectStorage in tests.
124:  */
125: export interface SharingStorage {
126:   collaborators: Collection<CollaboratorRecord>;
127:   shareKeys: Collection<ShareKeyRecord> & {
128:     /** A link's copies, keyed by the link they alias. */
129:     byAlias: NonUniqueIndex<ShareKeyRecord, string>;
130:   };
131: }
132: 
133: // Narrow a key record to a link, or undefined if it's an alias.
134: function asLink(record: ShareKeyRecord | undefined): ShareLinkRecord | undefined {
135:   return record !== undefined && record.alias === undefined ? record : undefined;
136: }
137: 
138: /**
139:  * Per-session caller identity. Mirrors the fields the OverseerClientInterface holds for the
140:  * connected client.
141:  */
142: export interface SharingCaller {
143:   /** The caller's profile.id (username/email). */
144:   profileId: string;
145:   /**
146:    * True if the caller is the gadget owner. The owner can manage anyone's collaborator edges
147:    * and share keys; non-owners are restricted to edges/keys they created themselves.
148:    */
149:   isOwner: boolean;
150: }
151: 
152: export class SharingManager {
153:   /**
154:    * `ownerProfileId` is stable for the lifetime of a gadget, so it's supplied once at
155:    * construction rather than per call.
156:    */
157:   constructor(private storage: SharingStorage, private ownerProfileId: string) {}
158: 
159:   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
160:   // Sharing-state queries
161: 
162:   /**
163:    * True if anyone other than the owner can currently access the gadget. Used by the Overseer's
164:    * `prohibitAllSharing` policy to decide whether a sensitive observation must be blocked.
165:    *
166:    * Because removed collaborators and revoked links linger in storage (the lazy revocation model;
167:    * see the module header and removeCollaborator/revokeShareLink), this must reflect *current*
168:    * reachability, not mere table membership: a collaborator with a live path from the owner, or
169:    * an un-revoked share link whose keys anyone could still redeem.
170:    */
171:   hasAnyShares(): boolean {
172:     if (this.computeEffectiveRoles().size > 0) return true;
173:     for (let link of this.#listLinks()) {
174:       if (!link.revoked) return true;
175:     }
176:     return false;
177:   }
178: 
179:   // Every share link, revoked or not. Aliases are skipped.
180:   *#listLinks(): Generator<ShareLinkRecord> {
181:     for (let record of this.storage.shareKeys.list()) {
182:       let link = asLink(record);
183:       if (link) yield link;
184:     }
185:   }
186: 
187:   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
188:   // Authorization (used by Overseer.open())
189: 
190:   /**
191:    * True if `profileId` currently has a collaborator record. This only checks membership; use
192:    * `getEffectiveRole()` to determine the actual access level (and whether the record is still
193:    * reachable from the owner in the permission graph).
194:    */
195:   isCollaborator(profileId: string): boolean {
196:     return this.storage.collaborators.get(profileId) !== undefined;
197:   }
198: 
199:   /**
200:    * The effective role of `profileId` -- the maximum role reachable from the owner through valid
201:    * permission edges -- or undefined if the user has no access. The owner always has "build".
202:    */
203:   getEffectiveRole(profileId: string): CollaboratorRole | undefined {
204:     if (profileId === this.ownerProfileId) return "build";
205:     return this.computeEffectiveRoles().get(profileId);
206:   }
207: 
208:   /**
209:    * Redeem a raw share key on behalf of a user opening the gadget. If the key exists, ensures the
210:    * user is a collaborator with a `shareKey` edge for its link (adding the edge if missing, or
211:    * creating the collaborator record if they're new). Does nothing if the key is unknown.
212:    *
213:    * The raw key is hashed internally; the plaintext is never stored. `fetchProfile` is invoked
214:    * (an RPC, in production) only when a brand-new collaborator must be created, so existing
215:    * collaborators are redeemed without any RPC.
216:    *
217:    * A key whose link is revoked behaves like an unknown key (it cannot be redeemed).
218:    */
219:   async redeemShareKey(opts: {
220:     rawKey: string;
221:     profileId: string;
222:     fetchProfile: () => Promise<AiChatAuthorInfo>;
223:   }): Promise<void> {
224:     let hash = await hashShareKey(opts.rawKey);
225:     let keyRecord = this.storage.shareKeys.get(hash);
226:     if (!keyRecord) return;
227: 
228:     // Edges point at the link, not the individual key, so a link's keys collapse to one grant.
229:     // A copy of a link is an alias; follow it to the link that owns the metadata.
230:     let link = keyRecord.alias === undefined
231:         ? keyRecord : asLink(this.storage.shareKeys.get(keyRecord.alias));
232:     if (!link || link.revoked) return;
233:     let linkId = link.id;
234:     let role = link.role ?? "build";
235: 
236:     let existing = this.storage.collaborators.get(opts.profileId);
237:     if (existing) {
238:       // User is already a collaborator. Only add an edge if they don't already have one for this
239:       // link (redeeming a second key of the same link is a no-op).
240:       let alreadyHasEdge = existing.addedBy.some(
241:           e => e.type === "shareKey" && e.keyId === linkId);
242:       if (!alreadyHasEdge) {
243:         existing.addedBy.push({
244:           type: "shareKey",
245:           keyId: linkId,
246:           created: new Date(),
247:           role,
248:         });
249:         this.storage.collaborators.put(existing);
250:       }
251:     } else {
252:       // New collaborator -- need full profile from their user DO.
253:       let profile = await opts.fetchProfile();
254:       this.storage.collaborators.put({
255:         profile,
256:         addedBy: [{
257:           type: "shareKey",
258:           keyId: linkId,
259:           created: new Date(),
260:           role,
261:         }],
262:       });
263:     }
264:   }
265: 
266:   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
267:   // Collaborator management
268: 
269:   /**
270:    * List currently-active collaborators -- those with a live path from the owner. Under the lazy
271:    * revocation model, removed collaborators linger in storage with no reachable role; they are
272:    * omitted here (they reappear if re-added).
273:    */
274:   listCollaborators(): CollaboratorInfo[] {
275:     let roles = this.computeEffectiveRoles();
276:     let result: CollaboratorInfo[] = [];
277:     for (let record of this.storage.collaborators.list()) {
278:       let role = roles.get(record.profile.id);
279:       if (!role) continue;  // not currently reachable from the owner
280:       result.push({
281:         profile: record.profile,
282:         addedBy: record.addedBy,
283:         role,
284:       });
285:     }
286:     return result;
287:   }
288: 
289:   /**
290:    * Add a collaborator with a `user` edge from the caller, granting `role`. The caller is
291:    * responsible for resolving `profile` (via RPC) and for any policy checks (e.g.
292:    * `prohibitAllSharing`). The caller may not grant a role higher than their own effective role.
293:    */
294:   addCollaborator(opts: {
295:     caller: SharingCaller;
296:     profile: AiChatAuthorInfo;
297:     role: CollaboratorRole;
298:     note?: string;
299:   }): CollaboratorInfo {
300:     // Don't add the owner as a collaborator.
301:     if (opts.profile.id === this.ownerProfileId) {
302:       throw new Error("Cannot add the workspace owner as a collaborator.");
303:     }
304: 
305:     let callerRole = this.#requireCallerRole(opts.caller);
306:     if (roleRank(opts.role) > roleRank(callerRole)) {
307:       throw new Error("You cannot grant a role higher than your own.");
308:     }
309: 
310:     let existing = this.storage.collaborators.get(opts.profile.id);
311:     let edge: PermissionEdge = {
312:       type: "user",
313:       sharer: opts.caller.profileId,
314:       created: new Date(),
315:       role: opts.role,
316:       note: opts.note,
317:     };
318: 
319:     if (existing) {
320:       // Already a collaborator -- add an edge if they don't have one from this sharer, otherwise
321:       // upgrade the existing edge's role (never silently downgrade).
322:       let existingEdge = existing.addedBy.find(
323:           e => e.type === "user" && e.sharer === opts.caller.profileId);
324:       if (existingEdge && existingEdge.type === "user") {
325:         existingEdge.role = maxRole(edgeGrantedRole(existingEdge), opts.role);
326:         if (opts.note !== undefined) existingEdge.note = opts.note;
327:       } else {
328:         existing.addedBy.push(edge);
329:       }
330:       this.storage.collaborators.put(existing);
331:       return {
332:         profile: existing.profile,
333:         addedBy: existing.addedBy,
334:         role: this.computeEffectiveRoles().get(existing.profile.id) ?? opts.role,
335:       };
336:     }
337: 
338:     let record: CollaboratorRecord = {
339:       profile: opts.profile,
340:       addedBy: [edge],
341:     };
342:     this.storage.collaborators.put(record);
343:     return {
344:       profile: record.profile,
345:       addedBy: record.addedBy,
346:       role: this.computeEffectiveRoles().get(record.profile.id) ?? opts.role,
347:     };
348:   }
349: 
350:   previewRemoveCollaborator(caller: SharingCaller, profileId: string): AffectedCollaborator[] {
351:     let target = this.storage.collaborators.get(profileId);
352:     if (!target) return [];
353: 
354:     let baseline = this.computeEffectiveRoles();
355:     let modified = caller.isOwner
356:         ? this.computeEffectiveRoles({ removedUser: profileId })
357:         : this.computeEffectiveRoles({
358:             removedEdge: { target: profileId, sharer: caller.profileId } });
359: 
360:     return this.#computeAffected(baseline, modified);
361:   }
362: 
363:   /**
364:    * Remove a collaborator by severing the edges that grant them access. This is a *lazy* removal:
365:    * nothing cascades and no records are deleted. The target's record (and crucially, any edges
366:    * where the target is the *sharer* of access to others) is left intact, and dependents who lose
367:    * their only path to the owner simply become unreachable -- they are denied at open() time, not
368:    * pruned here. This makes the removal trivially reversible: re-adding the target (see
369:    * addCollaborator) restores the target and, transitively, everyone they had shared with.
370:    *
371:    *   - The owner severs *all* incoming edges to the target (owner-removal means "gone now").
372:    *   - A non-owner severs only their own `user` edge to the target; if the target retains other
373:    *     edges, they keep access (possibly at a lower role).
374:    *
375:    * `keepUsers` is optional re-root sugar: any listed dependent who would otherwise lose access or
376:    * be downgraded is granted a fresh edge from the caller at their prior role (see
377:    * `#reRootKeptUsers`). Returns the collaborators whose access actually changed (removed or
378:    * downgraded), excluding kept users.
379:    */
380:   removeCollaborator(
381:       caller: SharingCaller, profileId: string, keepUsers: string[]): AffectedCollaborator[] {
382:     let target = this.storage.collaborators.get(profileId);
383:     if (!target) {
384:       throw new Error("User is not a collaborator.");
385:     }
386: 
387:     // Permission check: owner can remove anyone; collaborators can only remove users
388:     // they themselves added.
389:     if (!caller.isOwner) {
390:       let hasEdgeFromCaller = target.addedBy.some(
391:           e => e.type === "user" && e.sharer === caller.profileId);
392:       if (!hasEdgeFromCaller) {
393:         throw new Error("You can only remove users that you added.");
394:       }
395:     }
396: 
397:     let baseline = this.computeEffectiveRoles();
398: 
399:     // Sever the edges that grant the target access. The record is retained even if it becomes
400:     // empty, so the target's own outgoing grants survive and the removal can be undone.
401:     if (caller.isOwner) {
402:       target.addedBy = [];
403:     } else {
404:       target.addedBy = target.addedBy.filter(
405:           e => !(e.type === "user" && e.sharer === caller.profileId));
406:     }
407:     this.storage.collaborators.put(target);
408: 
409:     this.#reRootKeptUsers(caller, baseline, new Set(keepUsers));
410: 
411:     return this.#computeAffected(baseline, this.computeEffectiveRoles());
412:   }
413: 
414:   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
415:   // Share link management
416: 
417:   // Enforce that `caller` may manage `link`: the owner can manage any link; a collaborator only
418:   // the links they created. `action` is the user-facing verb (e.g. "revoke", "edit", "copy").
419:   #requireLinkManager(caller: SharingCaller, link: ShareLinkRecord, action: string): void {
420:     if (!caller.isOwner && link.createdBy !== caller.profileId) {
421:       throw new Error(`You can only ${action} share links that you created.`);
422:     }
423:   }
424: 
425:   // Look up a link by id, throwing the caller-facing error if the id is unknown or names an alias..
426:   #requireLink(linkId: string): ShareLinkRecord {
427:     let link = asLink(this.storage.shareKeys.get(linkId));
428:     if (!link) {
429:       throw new Error("Share link not found.");
430:     }
431:     return link;
432:   }
433: 
434:   async createShareLink(
435:       opts: { caller: SharingCaller; role: CollaboratorRole; note?: string })
436:       : Promise<{ key: string; linkId: string }> {
437:     let callerRole = this.#requireCallerRole(opts.caller);
438:     if (roleRank(opts.role) > roleRank(callerRole)) {
439:       throw new Error("You cannot grant a role higher than your own.");
440:     }
441: 
442:     // The link is stored as its first key: the record is keyed by that key's hash.
443:     let { key, hash } = await this.#mintKey();
444:     this.storage.shareKeys.put({
445:       id: hash,
446:       note: opts.note,
447:       created: new Date(),
448:       createdBy: opts.caller.profileId,
449:       role: opts.role,
450:     });
451:     return { key, linkId: hash };
452:   }
453: 
454:   /** Mints another key for an existing link. */
455:   async newShareLinkKey(opts: { caller: SharingCaller; linkId: string }): Promise<{ key: string }> {
456:     let link = this.#requireLink(opts.linkId);
457:     if (link.revoked) {
458:       throw new Error("Share link not found.");
459:     }
460:     this.#requireLinkManager(opts.caller, link, "copy");
461: 
462:     // Re-check the ceiling: the caller's role may have dropped below the link's since it was
463:     // created, and a fresh key must never grant more than the caller currently has.
464:     let callerRole = this.#requireCallerRole(opts.caller);
465:     if (roleRank(link.role ?? "build") > roleRank(callerRole)) {
466:       throw new Error("You cannot grant a role higher than your own.");
467:     }
468: 
469:     let { key, hash } = await this.#mintKey();
470:     this.storage.shareKeys.put({ id: hash, alias: link.id });
471:     return { key };
472:   }
473: 
474:   // Generate a random 128-bit key, returning it along with the hash it is stored under. The caller
475:   // decides whether that hash keys a link or an alias.
476:   async #mintKey(): Promise<{ key: string; hash: string }> {
477:     let rawBytes = new Uint8Array(16);
478:     crypto.getRandomValues(rawBytes);
479:     let key = rawBytes.toHex();
480:     return { key, hash: await hashShareKey(key) };
481:   }
482: 
483:   /**
484:    * Active (non-revoked) share links. The Overseer maps each `createdBy` profile.id to a display
485:    * profile (which may require RPC) to produce `ShareLinkInfo`s; see `getCreatorProfile`.
486:    */
487:   listShareLinkRecords(): ShareLinkRecord[] {
488:     return [...this.#listLinks()].filter(link => !link.revoked);
489:   }
490: 
491:   /**
492:    * Resolve the display profile for a share link's creator using only locally-available data
493:    * (the collaborator table). Returns undefined if the creator is neither a current collaborator
494:    * nor matched here (e.g. the owner), in which case the Overseer resolves it via RPC. The final
495:    * fallback (a bare profile from the id) is also the Overseer's responsibility.
496:    */
497:   getCreatorProfile(createdBy: string): AiChatAuthorInfo | undefined {
498:     return this.storage.collaborators.get(createdBy)?.profile;
499:   }
500: 
501:   updateShareLink(caller: SharingCaller, linkId: string, note?: string): void {
502:     let link = this.#requireLink(linkId);
503:     this.#requireLinkManager(caller, link, "edit");
504: 
505:     link.note = note === undefined ? undefined : note.slice(0, 500);
506:     this.storage.shareKeys.put(link);
507:   }
508: 
509:   previewRevokeShareLink(caller: SharingCaller, linkId: string): AffectedCollaborator[] {
510:     let link = asLink(this.storage.shareKeys.get(linkId));
511:     if (!link) return [];
512:     this.#requireLinkManager(caller, link, "revoke");
513:     if (link.revoked) return [];
514: 
515:     let baseline = this.computeEffectiveRoles();
516:     let modified = this.computeEffectiveRoles({ revokedLinkId: linkId });
517:     return this.#computeAffected(baseline, modified);
518:   }
519: 
520:   /**
521:    * Revoke a share link by soft-revoking it (setting the `revoked` flag) rather than deleting it.
522:    * This is the lazy counterpart to removeCollaborator: the link record and every `shareKey` edge
523:    * referencing it stay intact (no dangling references), but the link contributes nothing to the
524:    * permission graph and its keys can no longer be redeemed. Its copies are deleted outright,
525:    * since no edge ever names an alias. Users who relied solely on it become unreachable and
526:    * are denied at open() time.
527:    *
528:    * `keepUsers` is optional re-root sugar, identical to removeCollaborator. Returns the
529:    * collaborators whose access actually changed (removed or downgraded), excluding kept users.
530:    */
531:   revokeShareLink(
532:       caller: SharingCaller, linkId: string, keepUsers: string[]): AffectedCollaborator[] {
533:     let link = this.#requireLink(linkId);
534:     this.#requireLinkManager(caller, link, "revoke");
535: 
536:     let baseline = this.computeEffectiveRoles();
537: 
538:     link.revoked = true;
539:     this.storage.shareKeys.put(link);
540: 
541:     // Revoking makes the copies useless, and nothing references them, so delete them.
542:     this.storage.shareKeys.byAlias.delete(link.id);
543: 
544:     this.#reRootKeptUsers(caller, baseline, new Set(keepUsers));
545: 
546:     return this.#computeAffected(baseline, this.computeEffectiveRoles());
547:   }
548: 
549:   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
550:   // Permission-graph engine
551: 
552:   /**
553:    * Compute the effective role of every collaborator -- the maximum role reachable from the owner
554:    * through valid permission edges. A collaborator absent from the returned map has no access.
555:    *
556:    * The owner is the implicit root at "build". Each edge grants min(edge role, sharer's effective
557:    * role):
558:    *   - A "user" edge's sharer is the owner (effective "build") or another collaborator.
559:    *   - A "shareKey" edge's "sharer" is the key's creator; the edge grants the key's role bounded
560:    *     by the creator's effective role.
561:    *
562:    * Optional modifications model a hypothetical change, used by the preview methods:
563:    *   - `removedUser`: a profileId treated as removed (excluded from the graph entirely).
564:    *   - `removedEdge`: a single user edge (target ← sharer) treated as removed.
565:    *   - `revokedLinkId`: a link treated as revoked (its edges contribute nothing).
566:    */
567:   computeEffectiveRoles(opts: {
568:     removedUser?: string | null;
569:     removedEdge?: { target: string; sharer: string } | null;
570:     revokedLinkId?: string | null;
571:   } = {}): Map<string, CollaboratorRole> {
572:     let removedUser = opts.removedUser ?? null;
573:     let removedEdge = opts.removedEdge ?? null;
574:     let revokedLinkId = opts.revokedLinkId ?? null;
575: 
576:     // Map linkId → {creator, role}, excluding revoked links (the persisted `revoked` flag, and the
577:     // hypothetical `revokedLinkId` used by preview).
578:     let linkInfo = new Map<string, { creator: string; role: CollaboratorRole }>();
579:     for (let link of this.#listLinks()) {
580:       if (link.id === revokedLinkId || link.revoked) continue;
581:       linkInfo.set(link.id, {
582:         creator: link.createdBy,
583:         role: link.role ?? "build",
584:       });
585:     }
586: 
587:     // All collaborators except the removed user.
588:     let allCollabs = new Map<string, CollaboratorRecord>();
589:     for (let record of this.storage.collaborators.list()) {
590:       if (record.profile.id !== removedUser) {
591:         allCollabs.set(record.profile.id, record);
592:       }
593:     }
594: 
595:     // Roles known so far.
596:     let eff = new Map<string, CollaboratorRole>();
597: 
598:     // Effective role of a potential sharer (the owner is the root at "build").
599:     let sharerRole = (id: string): CollaboratorRole | undefined =>
600:         id === this.ownerProfileId ? "build" : eff.get(id);
601: 
602:     // Fixed-point iteration. Roles only increase, so this converges.
603:     let changed = true;
604:     while (changed) {
605:       changed = false;
606:       for (let [id, record] of allCollabs) {
607:         let best: CollaboratorRole | undefined = eff.get(id);
608:         for (let edge of record.addedBy) {
609:           let granted: CollaboratorRole | undefined;
610:           if (edge.type === "shareKey") {
611:             let info = linkInfo.get(edge.keyId);
612:             if (!info) continue;  // link revoked or no longer exists
613:             let creatorRole = sharerRole(info.creator);
614:             if (!creatorRole) continue;
615:             granted = minRole(info.role, creatorRole);
616:           } else {
617:             // Skip the specifically-removed edge.
618:             if (removedEdge && id === removedEdge.target &&
619:                 edge.sharer === removedEdge.sharer) {
620:               continue;
621:             }
622:             if (edge.sharer === removedUser) continue;
623:             let upstream = sharerRole(edge.sharer);
624:             if (!upstream) continue;
625:             granted = minRole(edgeGrantedRole(edge), upstream);
626:           }
627:           if (granted && (!best || roleRank(granted) > roleRank(best))) {
628:             best = granted;
629:           }
630:         }
631:         if (best && best !== eff.get(id)) {
632:           eff.set(id, best);
633:           changed = true;
634:         }
635:       }
636:     }
637: 
638:     return eff;
639:   }
640: 
641:   // The caller's effective role, throwing if the caller has no access at all (which should not
642:   // happen for an authorized session).
643:   #requireCallerRole(caller: SharingCaller): CollaboratorRole {
644:     if (caller.isOwner) return "build";
645:     let role = this.computeEffectiveRoles().get(caller.profileId);
646:     if (!role) {
647:       throw new Error("You do not have permission to share this workspace.");
648:     }
649:     return role;
650:   }
651: 
652:   // Diff two effective-role maps, returning the collaborators whose access changed. A user is
653:   // affected if they had access in `baseline` and either lost it (newRole null) or were downgraded
654:   // (newRole lower than oldRole) in `modified`. Profiles/edges are read from current storage.
655:   #computeAffected(
656:       baseline: Map<string, CollaboratorRole>,
657:       modified: Map<string, CollaboratorRole>): AffectedCollaborator[] {
658:     let result: AffectedCollaborator[] = [];
659:     for (let [id, oldRole] of baseline) {
660:       let newRole = modified.get(id) ?? null;
661:       if (newRole !== null && roleRank(newRole) >= roleRank(oldRole)) {
662:         continue;  // unchanged or (shouldn't happen) upgraded
663:       }
664:       let record = this.storage.collaborators.get(id);
665:       if (!record) continue;
666:       result.push({
667:         profile: record.profile,
668:         addedBy: record.addedBy,
669:         oldRole,
670:         newRole,
671:       });
672:     }
673:     return result;
674:   }
675: 
676:   // Optional re-root sugar for removeCollaborator/revokeShareLink. Must be called *after* the

17:  * provider failures -- it reports them as a final assistant message with stopReason "error" --
18:  * so this converts that shape back into an exception for callers that expect one (the overseer's
19:  * turn error triage and the one-shot completion helpers).
20:  */
21: export class AgentTurnError extends Error {
22:   /** HTTP status of the failing request, when the handle observed a response for it. */
23:   readonly statusCode?: number;
24: 
25:   constructor(message: string, statusCode?: number) {
26:     super(message);
27:     this.statusCode = statusCode;
28:   }
29: }
30: 
31: /**
32:  * Best-effort HTTP status extraction for a failed request. pi reports provider failures as
33:  * error text only, and its onResponse callback never fires for a request the SDK failed (so
34:  * ModelHandle.lastResponse is unset then) -- but the provider SDKs' error messages conventionally
35:  * begin with the status code (e.g. "400 {...}"), which is enough for the overseer's triage
36:  * (report 5xx/unknown, skip expected 4xx).
37:  */
38: export function httpStatusFromError(errorMessage: string, handle: ModelHandle)
39:     : number | undefined {
40:   const match = /^(\d{3})\b/.exec(errorMessage.trim());
41:   if (match) return Number(match[1]);
42:   return handle.lastResponse?.status;
43: }

46:  * Run a single non-streaming-style completion against a ModelHandle and return the response
47:  * text. Used for one-shot calls: title generation, binding naming, compaction summaries, and
48:  * LanguageModelBinding.run. Always requests thinking off (one-shots should be quick, and none
49:  * of them benefit from extended thinking; pre-pi, these calls never configured thinking either).
50:  * Throws AgentTurnError on provider failure, or the abort reason when `signal` fired.
51:  */
52: export async function completeText(handle: ModelHandle, args: {
53:   systemPrompt?: string;
54:   /** Convenience: wraps into a single user message. Exactly one of `prompt`/`messages` required. */
55:   prompt?: string;
56:   messages?: Message[];
57:   maxTokens?: number;
58:   signal?: AbortSignal;
59: }): Promise<string> {
60:   const messages: Message[] = args.messages ??
61:       [{ role: "user", content: args.prompt ?? "", timestamp: Date.now() }];
62:   const stream = await handle.stream(handle.model, {
63:     systemPrompt: args.systemPrompt,
64:     messages,
65:   }, {
66:     maxTokens: args.maxTokens,
67:     signal: args.signal,
68:     thinking: false,

72:     // Surface a cancellation as the abort reason, like a directly-aborted request would.
73:     args.signal?.throwIfAborted();

122:   "openai-completions": openaiCompletionsStream as StreamFunction<Api, SimpleStreamOptions>,
123:   "google-generative-ai": googleGenerativeAiStream as StreamFunction<Api, SimpleStreamOptions>,
124: };
125: 
126: const ZERO_COST: ModelCost = { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 };
127: 
128: // Consult pi's builtin catalog for cost/compat metadata of a known model id. Unknown models are
129: // fine (synthesized with zero cost). Import per-provider, not providers/all.
130: function catalogModel(provider: AiModelConfig["provider"], modelId: string): Model<Api> | undefined {
131:   switch (provider) {
132:     case "anthropic": return (ANTHROPIC_MODELS as Record<string, Model<Api>>)[modelId];
133:     case "openai": return (OPENAI_MODELS as Record<string, Model<Api>>)[modelId];
134:     case "google": return (GOOGLE_MODELS as Record<string, Model<Api>>)[modelId];
135:     case "cloudflare": return (CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_MODELS as Record<string, Model<Api>>)[modelId];
136:     case "ollama": return undefined;
137:     default: return undefined;
138:   }
139: }
140: 
141: // Token limits for a synthesized model. SUGGESTED_MODELS remains authoritative (compaction
142: // budgets in agent-compaction.ts are computed from it and must not change); pi's catalog fills
143: // gaps for models we don't list, and unknown models get conservative defaults.
144: function modelTokenWindow(config: AiModelConfig, catalog: Model<Api> | undefined)
145:     : { contextWindow: number, maxTokens: number } {
146:   const suggested = SUGGESTED_MODELS[config.provider]?.[config.model];
147:   return {
148:     contextWindow: suggested?.contextWindow ?? catalog?.contextWindow ?? 128_000,
149:     maxTokens: suggested?.outputLimit ??
150:         (config.provider === "cloudflare" ? WORKERS_AI_OUTPUT_LIMIT : undefined) ??
151:         catalog?.maxTokens ?? 4096,
152:   };
153: }
154: 
155: // Compat flags for a Workers AI model reached over its OpenAI-compatible endpoint (direct REST
156: // or the gateway's workers-ai route). Matches pi's own generated Workers AI catalog entries.
157: function workersAiCompat(catalog: Model<Api> | undefined): OpenAICompletionsCompat {
158:   return {
159:     supportsStore: false,
160:     supportsDeveloperRole: false,
161:     supportsLongCacheRetention: false,
162:     ...(catalog?.compat as OpenAICompletionsCompat | undefined),
163:     sendSessionAffinityHeaders: true,
164:   };
165: }
166: 
167: // Build the pi model descriptor for reaching a provider's own native API through an AI Gateway
168: // (the platform's or a user's). `gatewayUrl` is a gateway root -- over HTTPS
169: // (https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/{accountId}/{gateway}) or, for binding-routed requests,
170: // over the AI binding (https://workers-binding.ai/ai-gateway/gateways/{gateway}); each
171: // provider's native API is exposed under the same per-provider path on either. AI Gateway also
172: // offers a unified OpenAI-compat
173: // translation layer (/compat), which we deliberately never use: we already speak every
174: // provider's native API, and the translation drops provider features pi relies on (extended
175: // thinking, Anthropic cache_control prompt caching, the OpenAI Responses API). Billing --
176: // including unified billing on a user's own gateway -- is orthogonal to which API a request
177: // speaks. Returns undefined for providers AI Gateway cannot serve (ollama).
178: function gatewayNativeModel(config: AiModelConfig, gatewayUrl: string): Model<Api> | undefined {
179:   const catalog = catalogModel(config.provider, config.model);
180:   const window = modelTokenWindow(config, catalog);
181:   switch (config.provider) {
182:     case "anthropic":
183:       return {
184:         id: config.model,
185:         name: catalog?.name ?? config.model,
186:         api: "anthropic-messages",
187:         provider: "anthropic",
188:         baseUrl: `${gatewayUrl}/anthropic`,
189:         reasoning: true,
190:         input: catalog?.input ?? ["text", "image"],
191:         cost: catalog?.cost ?? ZERO_COST,
192:         ...window,
193:         thinkingLevelMap: catalog?.thinkingLevelMap,
194:         // Catalog compat verbatim: pi's catalog marks exactly the models that require the
195:         // adaptive thinking format (forceAdaptiveThinking); forcing it here breaks models that
196:         // don't support it (Haiku). Uncataloged model ids get budget-format thinking config --
197:         // if a new adaptive-only model isn't yet in pi's catalog, bump pi.
198:         compat: catalog?.compat,
199:       };
200:     case "openai":
201:       return {
202:         id: config.model,
203:         name: catalog?.name ?? config.model,
204:         api: "openai-responses",
205:         provider: "openai",
206:         baseUrl: `${gatewayUrl}/openai`,
207:         reasoning: catalog?.reasoning ?? true,
208:         input: catalog?.input ?? ["text", "image"],
209:         cost: catalog?.cost ?? ZERO_COST,
210:         ...window,
211:         thinkingLevelMap: catalog?.thinkingLevelMap,
212:         compat: catalog?.compat,
213:       };
214:     case "google":
215:       // pi's own gateway catalog skips Google, but the gateway's google-ai-studio passthrough +
216:       // pi's google API impl work; we construct the model ourselves. The @google/genai SDK
217:       // treats baseUrl as already including the version path.
218:       return {
219:         id: config.model,
220:         name: catalog?.name ?? config.model,
221:         api: "google-generative-ai",
222:         provider: "google",
223:         baseUrl: `${gatewayUrl}/google-ai-studio/v1beta`,
224:         reasoning: catalog?.reasoning ?? true,
225:         input: catalog?.input ?? ["text", "image"],
226:         cost: catalog?.cost ?? ZERO_COST,
227:         ...window,
228:         thinkingLevelMap: catalog?.thinkingLevelMap,
229:       };
230:     case "cloudflare":
231:       // Workers AI's own OpenAI-compatible endpoint, exposed through the gateway's workers-ai
232:       // route. This is Workers AI's native chat API (the same surface as its direct
233:       // /accounts/{id}/ai/v1 REST endpoint), not the gateway's cross-provider /compat layer.
234:       return {
235:         id: config.model,
236:         name: catalog?.name ?? config.model,
237:         api: "openai-completions",
238:         provider: "cloudflare-workers-ai",
239:         baseUrl: `${gatewayUrl}/workers-ai/v1`,
240:         reasoning: catalog?.reasoning ?? false,
241:         input: catalog?.input ?? ["text"],
242:         cost: catalog?.cost ?? ZERO_COST,
243:         ...window,
244:         compat: workersAiCompat(catalog),
245:       };
246:     default:
247:       return undefined;
248:   }
249: }

251: // Case-insensitive response-header lookup (pi surfaces headers as a plain record).
252: function getHeader(headers: Record<string, string>, name: string): string | undefined {
253:   if (headers[name] !== undefined) return headers[name];
254:   const lower = name.toLowerCase();
255:   for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(headers)) {
256:     if (key.toLowerCase() === lower) return value;
257:   }
258:   return undefined;
259: }
260: 
261: type HandleArgs = {
262:   model: Model<Api>;
263:   // Provider auth: a plain API key (pi turns it into the SDK's native auth) and/or headers.
264:   // A null header value suppresses a default header ({Authorization: null, "x-api-key": null}
265:   // alongside cf-aig-authorization makes pi skip SDK auth entirely).
266:   apiKey?: string;
267:   headers?: ProviderHeaders;
268:   // Structured gateway attribution; sent as `cf-aig-metadata` on gateway-routed requests only
269:   // (pi does not forward options.metadata to that header itself).
270:   gatewayMetadata?: GatewayMetadata;
271:   sessionAffinity?: string;
272:   aiGatewayLogRoute?: AiGatewayLogRoute;
273:   // Transport override for every request on this handle: how a binding-routed model reaches the
274:   // gateway over env.WORKERS_AI.fetch() instead of the global fetch (see bindingFetch).
275:   // A per-call options.fetch still wins, which tests rely on to capture requests.
276:   fetch?: FetchFunction;
277: };
278: 
279: function makeHandle(args: HandleArgs): ModelHandle {
280:   const streamFn = API_STREAMS[args.model.api];
281:   if (!streamFn) {
282:     throw new Error(`Unsupported model API "${args.model.api}".`);
283:   }
284: 
285:   // Per-API extras:
286:   // - Anthropic: adaptive thinking (the model decides when/how much to think)` -- but only for
287:   //   models pi's catalog marks adaptive-capable (compat.forceAdaptiveThinking). For other
288:   //   Anthropic models (e.g. Haiku 4.5, which rejects the adaptive format) we pass nothing, so pi
289:   //   omits the `thinking` field and the provider default (no extended thinking) applies --
290:   //   matching the pre-pi quick-model behavior.
291:   // - OpenAI Responses: explicit medium reasoning effort. pi would otherwise *disable* reasoning
292:   //   when no effort is passed; effort selection also makes pi request encrypted reasoning
293:   //   content, which -- with pi's unconditional `store: false` -- preserves the old stateless
294:   //   ZDR behavior with reasoning carried between tool steps.
295:   // - Everything else: provider defaults.
296:   const anthropicCompat = args.model.compat as AnthropicMessagesCompat | undefined;
297:   const apiExtras: Record<string, unknown> =
298:       args.model.api === "anthropic-messages"
299:           ? (anthropicCompat?.forceAdaptiveThinking === true ? { thinkingEnabled: true } : {}) :
300:       args.model.api === "openai-responses" ? { reasoningEffort: "medium" } : {};
301: 
302:   const handle: ModelHandle = {
303:     model: args.model,
304:     aiGatewayLogRoute: args.aiGatewayLogRoute,
305:     stream: (model, context, { thinking = true, ...options } = {}) => {
306:       // Never let a failed request read a previous request's response metadata.
307:       handle.lastResponse = undefined;
308:       const headers: ProviderHeaders = {
309:         ...args.headers,
310:         ...options.headers,
311:         ...(args.gatewayMetadata
312:             ? { "cf-aig-metadata": JSON.stringify(args.gatewayMetadata) }
313:             : {}),
314:       };
315:       const merged: SimpleStreamOptions = {
316:         // API defaults first, so an explicit per-call option can override them. `thinking: false`
317:         // replaces them with an explicit thinking-off request: for Anthropic pi sends
318:         // `thinking: {type:"disabled"}` (and knows to omit it for models that can't turn thinking
319:         // off, e.g. claude-fable-5); for OpenAI Responses, passing no reasoningEffort makes pi
320:         // disable reasoning.
321:         ...(thinking
322:             ? apiExtras
323:             : args.model.api === "anthropic-messages" ? { thinkingEnabled: false } : {}),
324:         ...(args.fetch !== undefined ? { fetch: args.fetch } : {}),
325:         ...options,
326:         ...(args.apiKey !== undefined ? { apiKey: args.apiKey } : {}),
327:         ...(Object.keys(headers).length > 0 ? { headers } : {}),
328:         // Session affinity: pi only sends it when caching isn't "none" (fine for us).
329:         sessionId: options.sessionId ?? args.sessionAffinity,
330:         onResponse: async (response, responseModel) => {
331:           handle.lastResponse = {
332:             status: response.status,
333:             aiGatewayLogId: getHeader(response.headers, "cf-aig-log-id"),
334:           };
335:           await options.onResponse?.(response, responseModel);
336:         },
337:         // PDF attachments ride pi image parts and are rewritten here into the provider's native
338:         // document blocks (no-op for payloads without one; see chat-attachment-pdf.ts).
339:         onPayload: async (payload, payloadModel) => {
340:           const replaced = await options.onPayload?.(payload, payloadModel);
341:           return bridgePdfAttachments(args.model.api, replaced ?? payload) ?? replaced;
342:         },
343:       };
344:       return streamFn(model, context, merged);
345:     },
346:   };
347:   return handle;
348: }
349: 
350: /**
351:  * Resolve an AiModelConfig to a ModelHandle, choosing among three routing modes: the user's own
352:  * AI Gateway (BYOK unified billing), the platform's AI Gateway (free tier), or direct provider
353:  * access with the config's own credentials. The handle carries the matching AI Gateway log route
354:  * for cost accounting, when there is one.
355:  */
356: export function getModel(env: Cloudflare.Env, config: AiModelConfig,
357:                          initiator: AiChatAuthorInfo,
358:                          options: ModelRoutingOptions = {}): ModelHandle {
359:   // BYOK: a connected user's own Cloudflare account pays for everything (all providers, including
360:   // Workers AI), routed through the user's own AI Gateway with unified billing. Honored regardless
361:   // of whether a platform AI Gateway is configured, so connected users are always billed correctly.
362:   if (options.userGateway) {
363:     return getModelViaUserGateway(
364:         config, buildMetadata(initiator, options.metadata), options.userGateway,
365:         options.sessionAffinity);
366:   }
367: 
368:   // Otherwise: when a platform AI Gateway is configured, route through it (platform-funded free
369:   // tier). The config's apiToken/apiUrl are ignored in that mode.
370:   let gwConfig = getAiGatewayConfig(env);
371:   if (gwConfig) {
372:     return getModelViaGateway(gwConfig, config, initiator, options);
373:   }
374: 
375:   return getModelDirect(config, options.sessionAffinity);
376: }
377: 
378: // Route inference through the user's own account (unified billing) via their account's default AI
379: // Gateway. Supports every provider AI Gateway serves, including Workers AI. Billed to the
380: // user's Cloudflare credits; no provider API key required.
381: function getModelViaUserGateway(
382:   config: AiModelConfig,
383:   metadata: GatewayMetadata,
384:   userGateway: UserGatewayRouting,
385:   sessionAffinity?: string,
386: ): ModelHandle {
387:   // Route through the user's AI Gateway data plane, speaking each provider's native API (see
388:   // gatewayNativeModel; unified *billing* has no API requirements). Auth is the connected user's
389:   // Cloudflare token via `cf-aig-authorization` (authorized by its `aig.run` scope); the
390:   // account-level `/ai/v1` REST endpoint rejects that token. We always use the account's
391:   // auto-created "default" gateway.
392:   const model = gatewayNativeModel(
393:       config, `https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/${userGateway.accountId}/default`);
394:   if (!model) {
395:     throw new Error(`Provider "${config.provider}" is not supported via unified billing.`);
396:   }
397:   return makeHandle({
398:     model,
399:     // The Google SDK requires an API key and sends it as `x-goog-api-key`, which the gateway
400:     // forwards verbatim unless it recognizes the token as gateway auth -- same stored-key flow
401:     // as the platform path (see getModelViaGateway).
402:     ...(config.provider === "google" ? { apiKey: userGateway.apiKey } : {}),
403:     headers: {
404:       "cf-aig-authorization": `Bearer ${userGateway.apiKey}`,
405:       Authorization: null,
406:       "x-api-key": null,
407:     },
408:     gatewayMetadata: metadata,
409:     sessionAffinity,
410:     aiGatewayLogRoute: {
411:       gateway: "default",
412:       accountId: userGateway.accountId,
413:       apiToken: userGateway.apiKey,
414:     },
415:   });
416: }
417: 
418: /**
419:  * Placeholder auth value for binding-routed requests. pi's API impls require an API key or a
420:  * recognized auth header (authorization, x-api-key, cf-aig-authorization) before dispatch;
421:  * binding calls are pre-authenticated in-account, so this satisfies the check and the gateway
422:  * recognizes and strips it rather than treating it as a BYOK provider key.
423:  */
424: const CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_BINDING_AUTH_SENTINEL = "cloudflare-gateway-binding";
425: 
426: /**
427:  * `Ai#fetch` exists at runtime but @cloudflare/workers-types' `Ai` doesn't declare it, so the
428:  * binding is cast structurally to reach the passthrough.
429:  */
430: type AiFetchBinding = {
431:   fetch(input: Request | string | URL, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response>;
432: };
433: 
434: // pi drives the model's baseUrl, which already names the gateway route on the binding's host,
435: // so the binding's fetch passes through unchanged -- no URL rewriting needed.
436: function bindingFetch(binding: Ai): FetchFunction {
437:   return (input, init) => (binding as unknown as AiFetchBinding).fetch(input, init);
438: }
439: 
440: // Platform free-tier path: route through the deployment's configured AI Gateway (platform-funded).
441: // Used only for requests that are NOT billed to a connected user's account.
442: function getModelViaGateway(
443:   gwConfig: AiGatewayConfig,
444:   config: AiModelConfig,
445:   initiator: AiChatAuthorInfo,
446:   options: ModelRoutingOptions,
447: ): ModelHandle {
448:   const metadata = buildMetadata(initiator, options.metadata);
449:   const binding = gwConfig.bindingFor(config.provider);
450:   // No binding means either the provider can't ride one or the deployment has none; the second
451:   // case already required a token in the constructor, so this only fires for the first
452:   if (!binding && !gwConfig.apiToken) {
453:     throw new Error(`Provider "${config.provider}" cannot use the Workers AI binding transport, ` +
454:         "and no CF_AI_GATEWAY_API_TOKEN is configured for the HTTPS one.");
455:   }
456:   const gatewayAuthHeaders: ProviderHeaders = {
457:     // pi's API impls explicitly recognize cf-aig-authorization and skip SDK auth; the null
458:     // values suppress the SDKs' own auth headers so the gateway's server-managed provider keys
459:     // apply.
460:     "cf-aig-authorization":
461:         `Bearer ${binding ? CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_BINDING_AUTH_SENTINEL : gwConfig.apiToken}`,
462:     Authorization: null,
463:     "x-api-key": null,
464:   };
465:   const gatewayBase =
466:       `https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/${gwConfig.accountId}`;
467:   // Cost-log reads are same-account, so the binding arm applies whenever the binding transport
468:   // is active (gwConfig.binding is unset when CF_AI_GATEWAY_USE_BINDING=false opts out) --
469:   // even for Google inference, which itself rides HTTPS (see AiGatewayConfig.bindingFor).
470:   const logRoute = (gateway: string): AiGatewayLogRoute => gwConfig.binding
471:       ? { gateway }
472:       : { gateway, accountId: gwConfig.accountId, apiToken: gwConfig.apiToken! };
473: 
474:   // Every provider -- Workers AI included -- rides the same gateway, with the same log route
475:   // and attribution metadata. Binding-routed providers address it on the binding's host, which
476:   // takes no account id (the binding channel carries identity); the paths are otherwise the
477:   // same, so the model descriptors are built identically from either root.
478:   const gateway = gwConfig.gateway;
479:   const gatewayUrl = binding
480:       ? `https://workers-binding.ai/ai-gateway/gateways/${gateway}`
481:       : `${gatewayBase}/${gateway}`;
482:   const model = gatewayNativeModel(config, gatewayUrl);
483:   if (!model) {
484:     throw new Error(
485:       `Provider "${config.provider}" is not supported through AI Gateway. ` +
486:       `Configured providers: ${[...gwConfig.providers].join(", ")}`
487:     );
488:   }
489: 
490:   return makeHandle({
491:     model,
492:     // The google API impl requires an apiKey (it doesn't recognize header-owned auth), and the
493:     // @google/genai SDK sends it as `x-goog-api-key` on every request -- which AI Gateway treats
494:     // as a provider key and forwards to Google verbatim, bypassing the gateway's server-managed
495:     // keys (credential precedence gives a request-supplied provider key top priority). The
496:     // documented stored-key flow for this SDK is to pass the *gateway token* as the SDK API key:
497:     // the gateway recognizes its own token there and applies the stored Google key instead.
498:     ...(config.provider === "google" ? { apiKey: gwConfig.apiToken } : {}),
499:     headers: gatewayAuthHeaders,
500:     ...(binding ? { fetch: bindingFetch(binding) } : {}),
501:     gatewayMetadata: metadata,
502:     sessionAffinity: options.sessionAffinity,
503:     aiGatewayLogRoute: logRoute(gateway),
504:   });
505: }
506: 
507: // Direct provider access using the credentials in the model config itself (no AI Gateway).
508: function getModelDirect(config: AiModelConfig, sessionAffinity?: string): ModelHandle {
509:   const catalog = catalogModel(config.provider, config.model);
510:   const window = modelTokenWindow(config, catalog);
511:   switch (config.provider) {
512:     case "anthropic":
513:       return makeHandle({
514:         model: {
515:           id: config.model,
516:           name: catalog?.name ?? config.model,
517:           api: "anthropic-messages",
518:           provider: "anthropic",
519:           baseUrl: config.apiUrl ?? "https://api.anthropic.com",
520:           reasoning: true,
521:           input: catalog?.input ?? ["text", "image"],
522:           cost: catalog?.cost ?? ZERO_COST,
523:           ...window,
524:           thinkingLevelMap: catalog?.thinkingLevelMap,
525:           // Catalog compat verbatim -- see the gateway-path comment on forceAdaptiveThinking.
526:           compat: catalog?.compat,
527:         },
528:         apiKey: config.apiToken,
529:         sessionAffinity,
530:       });
531:     case "cloudflare": {
532:       // Workers AI is fetch-only (no Workers-binding transport), so outside AI Gateway mode it's
533:       // BYOK like every other provider: the user's own account ID and API token come from the
534:       // model config. (The REST endpoint is account-scoped, hence the extra accountId field.)
535:       if (!config.accountId || !config.apiToken) {
536:         throw new Error(
537:             "This Workers AI model has no Cloudflare credentials. Re-add it with your " +
538:             "Cloudflare account ID and an API token that permits Workers AI.");
539:       }
540:       return makeHandle({
541:         model: {
542:           id: config.model,
543:           name: catalog?.name ?? config.model,
544:           api: "openai-completions",
545:           provider: "cloudflare-workers-ai",
546:           baseUrl: `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/${config.accountId}/ai/v1`,
547:           reasoning: catalog?.reasoning ?? false,
548:           input: catalog?.input ?? ["text"],
549:           cost: catalog?.cost ?? ZERO_COST,
550:           ...window,
551:           compat: workersAiCompat(catalog),
552:         },
553:         apiKey: config.apiToken,
554:         sessionAffinity,
555:       });
556:     }
557:     case "google":
558:       return makeHandle({
559:         model: {
560:           id: config.model,
561:           name: catalog?.name ?? config.model,
562:           api: "google-generative-ai",
563:           provider: "google",
564:           baseUrl: config.apiUrl ?? "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta",
565:           reasoning: catalog?.reasoning ?? true,
566:           input: catalog?.input ?? ["text", "image"],
567:           cost: catalog?.cost ?? ZERO_COST,
568:           ...window,
569:           thinkingLevelMap: catalog?.thinkingLevelMap,
570:         },
571:         apiKey: config.apiToken,
572:         sessionAffinity,
573:       });
574:     case "ollama":
575:       // `apiUrl` is the Ollama server base; its OpenAI-compat endpoint lives under /v1. Accept
576:       // (and strip) a trailing `/api` or `/v1` path: configs saved before the pi migration store
577:       // the native-API base `http://host:11434/api` (the old ollama provider's convention), and
578:       // users may paste the /v1 endpoint directly. When no API key was configured we assume
579:       // local auth and send no Authorization header at all (as before the pi migration; a strict
580:       // local proxy may reject an unexpected bearer token): the OpenAI SDK requires *some* key,
581:       // so give it a placeholder while a null default header deletes the Authorization header
582:       // the SDK derives from it.
583:       return makeHandle({
584:         model: {
585:           id: config.model,
586:           name: config.model,
587:           api: "openai-completions",
588:           provider: "ollama",
589:           baseUrl: `${stripTrailingSlashes(config.apiUrl ?? "http://localhost:11434")
590:               .replace(/\/(api|v1)$/, "")}/v1`,
591:           reasoning: true,
592:           input: ["text", "image"],
593:           cost: ZERO_COST,
594: 
595:           // Pi's OpenAI compat uses the "developer" role for the system prompt by default,
596:           // disabling it only for certain hostnames which are known not to support it.
597:           //
598:           // In ollama, some models support it and some do not. Frustratingly, the ones that do not
599:           // don't necessarily throw an error. They may just proceed without a system prompt. For
600:           // example, when I tested Muse Glimmer the day after it was released, I found it
601:           // understood what tool calls were available to it but didn't know any of the info in
602:           // the system prompt. Annoyingly, Muse Glimmer seems to be trained to treat the system
603:           // prompt as secret, so refused to answer my questions about it directly. But I figured
604:           // out it clearly wasn't getting the system prompt. And when I disabled  the "developer"
605:           // role, the problem was fixed. In contrast, though, Gemma 4 running under otherwise
606:           // exactly the same setup does understand the "developer" role and works fine. Weird!
607:           //
608:           // Some users also filed issues about this because they were trying to use the ollama
609:           // provider as a way to target an arbitrary third-party OpenAI-compatible provider. This
610:           // is not the intended use case for the ollama provider -- we should add an explicit
611:           // provider for this. The ollama provider could in the future switch to using the ollama
612:           // native API rather than the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which would break users using
613:           // it in this way. That said, if this flag works as a temporary work-around for them
614:           // util we add a real OpenAI provider option... great.
615:           compat: catalog?.compat ?? {supportsDeveloperRole: false},
616: 
617:           ...window,
618:         },
619:         ...(config.apiToken === ""
620:             ? { apiKey: "unused", headers: { Authorization: null } }
621:             : { apiKey: config.apiToken }),
622:         sessionAffinity,

2: // whether a user's request may proceed, and whose credentials to use.
3: //
4: // Billing rules (see canProceedWithRequest):

6: //     counter is NOT consumed (the platform free tier is reserved for everyone else).

8: //     daily counter is consumed and, once exhausted, the request is blocked.

20:   /** Guidance/reason when blocked. */
21:   reason?: string;
22:   /** Whether to serve the request using the user's own gateway/keys rather than the platform's. */
23:   shouldUseByok: boolean;
24:   /** Whether the user is within their free-tier limit. */
25:   withinLimits: boolean;

44: // Result used when limits are disabled (self-hosted / unlimited).

64: export async function checkUsageAndBalance(
65:   env: Cloudflare.Env,
66:   userStub: DurableObjectStub<UserDurableObject>,

73:   const minimumBalance = getMinimumCloudflareBalance(env);

1: // Resolves AI Gateway billing state for a user's connected Cloudflare account.
2: //
3: // The OAuth tokens live in the connected Cloudflare *gatekeeper* account; we obtain a usable access
4: // token from it (getUsableAccessToken), then resolve which account to bill and read the credit
5: // balance (with a short cache). Connected-user inference is routed through the account's auto-created
6: // "default" AI Gateway (see ai-models.ts), billed via Unified Billing.
7: //
8: // Operates against a UserDurableObject stub so it can be called from the overseer (usage checks) and
9: // from the RPC layer (status display).
10: 
11: import { listAccounts, fetchCreditBalance } from "./account-service.js";
12: import type { UserDurableObject } from "../../user.js";
13: 
14: // Treat a cached balance as fresh for this long.
15: const CREDITS_CACHE_TTL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;
16: 
17: type UserStub = DurableObjectStub<UserDurableObject>;
18: 
19: /** Public-safe connection status for display and for the usage decision. */
20: export interface CloudflareConnectionStatus {
21:   connected: boolean;
22:   accountId?: string;
23:   accountName?: string;
24:   balance: number | null;
25:   /**
26:    * True when connected but the grant sees multiple Cloudflare accounts and none is chosen yet.
27:    * The client must prompt the user to select one via selectAccount().
28:    */
29:   needsAccountSelection?: boolean;
30: }
31: 
32: /** A Cloudflare account the connected grant can access. */
33: export interface CloudflareAccountOption {
34:   accountId: string;
35:   accountName: string;
36: }
37: 
38: /**
39:  * Routing details to bill a user's own Cloudflare account for inference (BYOK path once the free
40:  * tier is spent). Inference is routed through the account's "default" AI Gateway.
41:  */
42: export interface ByokGatewayRouting {
43:   accountId: string;
44:   /** The user's Cloudflare access token, used as the authorization. */
45:   apiKey: string;
46: }
47: 
48: /**
49:  * Connection resolution result. `accessToken`/`accountId` are present only when connected with a
50:  * resolved account; `accessToken` is sensitive (never send it to the client).
51:  */
52: export interface ResolvedConnection {
53:   status: CloudflareConnectionStatus;
54:   accessToken?: string;
55:   accountId?: string;
56: }
57: 
58: // Get a usable access token from the connected Cloudflare gatekeeper account, or null if the user
59: // hasn't connected Cloudflare or the connection is broken/expired.
60: async function getUsableAccessToken(userStub: UserStub): Promise<string | null> {
61:   // The returned stub is a server-side RPC stub (not an auto-disposed call parameter), so it must be
62:   // disposed to avoid leaking on every call (this runs on the hot path — see resolveConnection).
63:   using account = await userStub.getCloudflareGatekeeperAccount();
64:   if (!account) return null;
65:   return await account.getUsableAccessToken();
66: }
67: 
68: /**
69:  * Resolve connection status + balance (cached when fresh), auto-selecting the account when exactly
70:  * one is accessible. Also surfaces the usable access token + resolved account id so a hot-path
71:  * caller can derive BYOK routing without re-reading. Never throws; returns a safe default.
72:  */
73: export async function resolveConnection(
74:   _env: Cloudflare.Env, userStub: UserStub,
75: ): Promise<ResolvedConnection> {
76:   try {
77:     // Dispose the connected-account stub at the end of this call (it's a returned RPC stub, not an
78:     // auto-disposed parameter). This runs on every agent turn and UI refresh.
79:     using account = await userStub.getCloudflareGatekeeperAccount();
80:     if (!account) return { status: { connected: false, balance: null } };
81: 
82:     const accessToken = await account.getUsableAccessToken();
83:     if (!accessToken) {
84:       // Connected, but the token is broken/expired — treat as connected with unknown balance.
85:       return { status: { connected: true, balance: null } };
86:     }
87: 
88:     const billing = await userStub.getCloudflareBilling();
89:     let accountId = billing?.accountId;
90:     let accountName = billing?.accountName;
91:     let needsAccountSelection = false;
92:     if (!accountId) {
93:       const accounts = await listAccounts(accessToken);
94:       if (accounts.length === 1) {
95:         accountId = accounts[0].accountId;
96:         accountName = accounts[0].accountName;
97:         await userStub.setCloudflareAccountSelection(accountId, accountName);
98:       } else if (accounts.length > 1) {
99:         needsAccountSelection = true;
100:       }
101:     }
102: 
103:     const base = { connected: true as const, accountId, accountName, needsAccountSelection };
104:     const extra = { accessToken, accountId };
105: 
106:     // Serve a fresh cached balance without hitting the API.
107:     const cacheAge = billing?.creditsUpdatedAt ? Date.now() - billing.creditsUpdatedAt : Infinity;
108:     if (cacheAge < CREDITS_CACHE_TTL_MS && billing?.creditsRemaining !== undefined) {
109:       return { status: { ...base, balance: billing.creditsRemaining ?? null }, ...extra };

142:     const accountId = billing?.accountId;
143:     if (!accountId) return;
144:     const fresh = await fetchCreditBalance(token, accountId);
145:     if (fresh !== null) await userStub.updateCloudflareCredits(fresh);
146:   } catch {
147:     // Best effort — leave the cached value in place.
148:   }
149: }

157:     if (!token) return [];
158:     return await listAccounts(token);

161:   }

40:     stub: T, log: ReturnType<typeof createWorkshopLogger> = logger): T {
41:   return new Proxy(stub, {
42:     get(target, prop) {
43:       const value = Reflect.get(target, prop) as unknown;
44:       if (typeof value !== "function") return value;
45:       // Invoke through the stub (`target[prop](...)`) rather than `.apply` on the extracted
46:       // handle: native RPC method handles are themselves proxies, and touching `.apply` on one
47:       // is interpreted as a nested RPC property access (the DO then rejects a call to "apply").
48:       const methods = target as unknown as Record<PropertyKey, (...a: unknown[]) => unknown>;
49:       if (typeof prop !== "string") return (...args: unknown[]) => methods[prop](...args);
50:       return (...args: unknown[]) => {
51:         const result = methods[prop](...args);
52:         if (typeof (result as PromiseLike<unknown> | undefined)?.then !== "function") return result;
53:         return (async () => {
54:           try {
55:             return await (result as PromiseLike<unknown>);
56:           } catch (e) {
57:             if (isDoResetError(e)) {
58:               log.warn("user DO reset observed", {
59:                 event: "user_do.reset.surfaced",
60:                 operation: prop,
61:                 durableObjectId: target.id.toString(),
62:                 error: e,
63:               });
64:             }
65:             throw e;
66:           }
67:         })();
68:       };
69:     },
70:   });
71: }
72: 
73: // Full jitter decorrelates the replay burst a mass reset produces (a reset fails every
74: // in-flight call from every session at once); workerd queues the fresh-stub request behind
75: // the object restart, so no delay floor is needed.
76: const RETRY_JITTER_MS = 250;
77: 
78: /** Whether a rejection may be retried, given a call already known to be replay-safe.
79:  * Narrower than `isDoResetError`: `durableObjectReset` retries even with `overloaded` set (the
80:  * incarnation is dead — the queue that overloaded it died with it; this is the shape production
81:  * storage-timeout resets arrive in), a deliberate divergence from the never-retry-`overloaded`
82:  * guidance in the error-handling docs linked above. Bare `retryable` (connection lost to a
83:  * possibly-live object) retries only if it isn't shedding load. */
84: function shouldRetryAfterReset(e: unknown): boolean {
85:   if (typeof e !== "object" || e === null) return false;
86:   const flags = e as { durableObjectReset?: unknown; retryable?: unknown; overloaded?: unknown };
87:   if (flags.durableObjectReset === true) return true;
88:   return flags.retryable === true && flags.overloaded !== true;
89: }
90: 
91: /** Retries `callWithFreshStub` once if it rejects with a DO-reset shape. The caller asserts the
92:  * call is replay-safe (a reset can't distinguish "never applied" from "applied, response lost")
93:  * — wrap pure reads only. The thunk must mint its stub inside itself (e.g. via the fresh-stub
94:  * getters) so the second attempt gets a fresh incarnation; a captured stub is permanently broken
95:  * and retrying it is a silent no-op. Pass the same logger the stub's `wrapDoStubForTelemetry`
96:  * uses so the recovery is attributed to the component (and context, e.g. gadgetId) whose
97:  * surfaced warning it absorbs; defaults to the Worker's. */
98: export async function retryOnDoReset<T>(
99:     callWithFreshStub: () => Promise<T>,
100:     log: ReturnType<typeof createWorkshopLogger> = logger): Promise<T> {
101:   try {
102:     return await callWithFreshStub();
103:   } catch (e) {
104:     if (!shouldRetryAfterReset(e)) throw e;  // identity rethrow, flags intact
105:     await scheduler.wait(Math.random() * RETRY_JITTER_MS);
106:     let recovered = await callWithFreshStub();  // a second rejection propagates by identity
107:     log.info("recovered from user DO reset", { event: "user_do.reset.recovered" });
108:     return recovered;
109:   }

3: // concurrent drains (the DO's input gate is open across the apply await) can't double-apply the

11: const logger = createWorkshopLogger("workshop.auto.approval");
12: 
13: export interface AutoApprovalStorage {
14:   actions: Collection<ActionRecord, number>
15:       & { pendingByGatekeeper: NonUniqueIndex<ActionRecord, number> };
16:   autoApproveTags: Collection<AutoApproveTagRecord>;
17: }
18: 
19: /**
20:  * Applies a single eligible pending action: invoke the gatekeeper, mark it approved, persist. The
21:  * caller has already validated that the record is still pending.
22:  */
23: export type ApplyPendingActionFn = (
24:     record: ActionRecord & {type: "action"},
25:     resolvedBy: AiChatAuthorInfo,
26:     autoApproved: boolean) => Promise<void>;
27: 
28: export class AutoApprovalDrainer {
29:   // Per-gatekeeper single-flight state. Key present => a drain is running for that gatekeeper; the
30:   // value is a "rerun" flag, set when another drain is requested while one is in flight, so work
31:   // submitted during a drain isn't lost.
32:   #draining = new Map<number, boolean>();
33: 
34:   constructor(
35:       private storage: AutoApprovalStorage,
36:       private applyPendingAction: ApplyPendingActionFn) {}
37: 
38:   async drain(gatekeeperId: number): Promise<void> {
39:     if (this.#draining.has(gatekeeperId)) {
40:       this.#draining.set(gatekeeperId, true);  // ask the running drain to loop again
41:       return;
42:     }
43:     this.#draining.set(gatekeeperId, false);
44:     try {
45:       do {
46:         this.#draining.set(gatekeeperId, false);
47:         await this.#drainOnce(gatekeeperId);
48:       } while (this.#draining.get(gatekeeperId));
49:     } finally {
50:       this.#draining.delete(gatekeeperId);
51:     }
52:   }
53: 
54:   // Apply all currently-eligible pending actions of the gatekeeper, in ascending id order. Stops
55:   // at the first pending action that is NOT auto-eligible (a manual gate) or that throws while
56:   // applying -- it is never skipped ahead of. This preserves in-order application and the
57:   // invariant that nothing is silently applied past a human gate.
58:   //
59:   // Eligibility requires BOTH signals: the author's `autoApprovable` verdict on the action AND a
60:   // user-enabled rule for the action's type on this gatekeeper.
61:   async #drainOnce(gatekeeperId: number): Promise<void> {
62:     // Materialize before applying: the index yields lazily in ascending id order, and applying
63:     // mutates it mid-iteration. Actions created after this snapshot trigger their own drain(),
64:     // which drain()'s rerun flag folds into this run if it's still in flight.
65:     let pending = [...this.storage.actions.pendingByGatekeeper.get(gatekeeperId)];
66: 
67:     for (let record of pending) {
68:       if (record.type !== "action") continue;
69: 
70:       let tag = record.description.actionKind?.tag;
71:       let rule = tag !== undefined
72:           ? this.storage.autoApproveTags.get(`${gatekeeperId}:${tag}`)
73:           : undefined;
74:       if (record.description.autoApprovable !== true || rule === undefined) {
75:         // A manual gate. Stop rather than skipping ahead to any later auto-eligible action.
76:         return;
77:       }
78: 
79:       // Re-check immediately before applying, to guard against a concurrent drain having already
80:       // taken this one.
81:       let fresh = this.storage.actions.get(record.id);
82:       if (!fresh || fresh.type !== "action" || fresh.state !== "pending") {
83:         continue;
84:       }
85: 
86:       try {
87:         // Attribute the auto-approval to the user who enabled the rule -- it runs under their
88:         // authority.
89:         await this.applyPendingAction(fresh, rule.enabledBy, true);
90:       } catch (err) {
91:         // Leave the action pending for manual handling and stop the drain (never skip ahead).
92:         logger.error("auto-approval failed", {
93:           event: "auto.approval.failed", actionId: fresh.id, error: err,
94:         });

96:       }

98:   }
